*Socket economy — flagged, not solved.* With one home-ship socket and a terminal `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN`, the first weld-then-cut leaves the ship with no free socket for the rest of the MVP slice. This is acceptable for the MVP slice (one weld scenario, concept MVP definition) and recorded as a Vertical Slice question to Modular Ship Assembly and the game-designer: either more sockets per home-ship, or a verb that re-cuts a `CAPPED` socket open again while leaving its history visible (old bead plus cut ring). The three options and the socket-economy formula are in Open Questions. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Consequence for the fantasy and the experience targets:** with one socket and one mate there is no *choice* of what to weld (only whether), so the claim that the crew chooses *what* to graft (Player Fantasy, X-3) is a Vertical Slice claim; and if OQ-1 is resolved before then, the design review's preferred answer is **option A** (a re-cut verb that reopens a `CAPPED` socket while leaving its history visible), because it is the only option that does not delete the scar the fantasy is built on.

**LY-14 — The mating predicate, `socket_plan` and `can_attach`.** Two sockets MATE iff all of the following hold; the verdict is the FIRST failing reason in this order (cheap before expensive; closed set, distinct from the Graph's): both exist (`SOCKET_UNKNOWN`); both are `FREE` (`SOCKET_NOT_FREE`); they lie on different bodies (`SAME_BODY`); facings are opposite (`FACING_MISMATCH`); `width_tiles` equal (`WIDTH_MISMATCH`); classes compatible (`CLASS_MISMATCH`; MVP: equal `class_id`); lane multisets equal by `(loop, lane_index)` (`LANE_MISMATCH`); and the translated footprints of the two bodies do not overlap (`GEOM_OVERLAP`, D.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The `GEOM_OVERLAP` test set is the STATIC footprint, not `rects_in`:** `rects_in` returns occluders in their current leaf state, so a low prop (SOLID, not occluding) would escape it, the verdict would flip as a door animates, and floor laid on floor would pass. The test therefore runs over (i) every static rect of both bodies with **all** flags (SOLID or not, occluding or not), each socket's PLATE slot counted at its full footprint (the maximal, FREE-state geometry) and no leaf or JAMB slot, (ii) the tile cells of every room of both bodies (rect against tile, and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell are both `GEOM_OVERLAP`), after the D.6 translation; abutting is legal. It uses the broadphase grid of each body and is **memoised on `(socket_a, socket_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`** (D.22), so a door animating on either body never invalidates or flips it. The mated PLATE footprints of the two sockets themselves abut at the seam line and do not overlap. **Order of the two verdicts (C-4):** Layout's `SOCKET_NOT_FREE` answers socket-level occupancy FIRST; the Graph's `SOCKET_OCCUPIED` (LSG:170) remains the port- and edge-level reason. Because `SAME_BODY` is a hard reject and every weld merges two bodies, the weld relation over sections is always a forest, so a cut always splits a body into exactly two components (no ring, no "cut that does not split").
*Geometry.* Mating is ABUT: the two 24-px hull walls sit side by side, the shared boundary is the seam line and the door frames are in line. The weld offset is `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b` (D.6). Every input of that sum lies on the 24-px grid (lint `GRID_24`, LY-30) and `offset_a` does too, so `offset_b` lies on the 24-px grid by construction (D.6): the closure needs no catalogue-wide socket phase, because rooms sit on per-room 24-px origins (LY-5). Any off-grid `offset_b` from a validated plan is a defect, not a reason code. The N/S double bulkhead's up-screen face arrangement is routed to the art-director (PIPE:794), not a Layout rule.
*`socket_plan(socket_a, socket_b) -> {pairs[], openings[], L_seam, reason}`* is a PURE query returning the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (LSG:170): `pairs[]` one per lane, `openings[]` one per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`. **Assembly adds `q` and issues the command; the Graph's `can_join(plan)` validates; both verdicts must pass before `apply`** *(Modular Ship Assembly is designed; MSA repeats this)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* This is the whole answer to the index's "three GDDs would each define a socket" (IDX:28): one record type, one mating rule, one plan builder. Lane matching is by `(loop, lane_index)` (positional within the socket), so a pipe never visibly kinks across the seam. A socket with no `hatch` is bulkhead-only (the weld joins lanes only; `openings[]` is empty). *(CLARIFY, orchestrator ruling: one-sided hatches.)* If exactly one of two mating sockets declares a hatch, the pair is legal and behaves as bulkhead-only: `openings[]` is empty, the hatched socket's hatch stays HULL (its PLATE slot stays active, as in `FREE`, LY-15) while the socket is `WELDED`, `socket_plan` raises the diagnostic `hatch_one_sided`, and no reason code is added (the closed set of LY-29 stands). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **The player must be able to read it before the weld spends the socket:** `hatch_one_sided` is part of the `can_attach` / `socket_plan` **preview payload** `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}`, and the weld cursor outline (UI Requirements) shows the one-sided side diegetically as a closed bulkhead outline with no hatch ring on the bare side — "no passage here" — so welding onto a hatchless mate is never a surprise (routed to Modular Ship Assembly and the art-director). Rejected: a mismatch reason (it would forbid welding a hatched home-ship dock to a derelict whose wreck lost its hatch, which is the common case) and an automatic hatch on the bare side (Layout never invents geometry). A hatch requires `width_tiles >= 2` and is **low-aligned**: its `doorway_start_px` equals the socket's `start_px` (lint `HATCH_WIDTH` checks the width and lint `HATCH_ALIGN` checks the alignment; the field is derived for a hatch door and any other authored value is the lint error `HATCH_ALIGN`). A 3-tile (144-px) socket holds one 96-px hatch plus 48 px of bulkhead on the HIGH side. Low alignment is what keeps the two hatches of a mate in line: spans coincide after the D.6 translation and "LOW" is the same side in both frames (LY-9), so no per-hatch offset can differ and no `HATCH_OFFSET_M

**LY-15 — Hatches: HULL before, ONE opening after.** Before mating, a socket's hatch is HULL: the socket's PLATE, a `SOLID | OCCLUDES_LIGHT | HULL` rect covering the **whole socket span** (`width_tiles × 48` along the run × 24 deep — for the MVP's 2-tile socket that span is exactly the 96-px doorway) and no Graph opening. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: one plate footprint, used by the table, the prose and the compile rule below.)* The weld creates ONE Graph OPENING per mated hatch pair with `area_max = min(a.area_max, b.area_max)`; both sections' hatch leaves are DOOR_LEAF rects driven by that one `area` (two rects, one truth, hinges fixed by LY-9). The leak itself belongs to the Graph (`A_CUT` 24 per former opening, hull stub `hp` 2500, LSG:172 — the Graph's hole, not a Layout rect).

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: this table is the socket-span variant matrix, replacing an earlier per-state table whose variant pieces had no reserved `idx`.)* It applies to a **hatched** socket of width `W` tiles (span `W × 48` px). **The socket-span compile (stated once; used by LY-4, LY-7, LY-30 and D.9).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* (a) The socket span is `[start_px, start_px + W × 48)` along its HULL run and must lie inside that one authored run (lint `SOCKET_ON_EXTERIOR`). (b) At template load the run is **split into three**: `[run start, start_px)` before the span, the span, and `[span end, run end)` after it. Before and after are ordinary static wall rects carrying the run's flags and each is omitted if its length is 0 (a 2-tile airlock socket that fills its whole run has neither); the span is **not** a static rect, so the plate never overlaps the wall (`RECT_OVERLAP` cannot fire) — the same "run compiles in parts, no SOLID overlap" precedent as the hull-port row of LY-7. (e) The pocket into which the leaf retracts is **presentation only** for a hatch: the leaf rect shrinks toward the LOW end and the retracted part is never a rect, so a hatch is **exempt from `DOOR_POCKET_CLEAR`** (the LOW-side pocket of D.18 would lie outside a 2-tile run, and no rect or clearance test depends on it); interior doors keep the pocket rule. (f) `exposed_tiles` is unchanged: D.4 counts the **authored** run's `len_tiles`, and the split is a compile step. (g) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: split, because the LEAF's extent depends on `area`, which is not a function of the socket.)* **Slot activation** (which of PLATE, JAMB and LEAF are *present*) is a pure function of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` — the table above — evaluated by LM1-LM4 and `post_restore`; the mate's hatch is known from the two templates, so the function needs no persisted field. **Leaf extent** (`leaf_w`, hence whether the present LEAF returns a rect) is a function of the opening's `area` (D.5), set by `layout.doors` in P3 — except that a LEAF newly activated by a weld (LM2) or by `post_restore` is initialised **closed** (`leaf_w = width_px`) and its last-projected cache seeded, so it is never absent before its first P3 derivation (LY-16, LY-26 d).

**LY-16 — Recording a weld.** `attach_section(socket_a, socket_b, seam_id, welded_at_T)` (LM2, Class A) runs after the Graph's `weld_join` inside Assembly's single `apply` (KRN:197: single commands "whose `apply` calls published mutators on Graph, Layout and Body"). It appends a `welds[]` row `{seam_id, section_a, socket_a, section_b, socket_b, welded_at_T, state ACTIVE}`; sets both sockets `WELDED(seam_id)`; re-bases every section of the absorbed body by D.6 and moves them onto the host body; marks the absorbed body `DISSOLVED`; switches the variant slots of both sockets (LY-15), **initialises each newly active LEAF closed (`leaf_w = width_px`, consistent with `weld_join`'s new opening starting at `area` 0, Assembly MSA-15) and seeds the last-projected `leaf_w` cache with that value in the same `apply`, so the hatch span is solid from the instant the PLATE switches off; `layout.doors` re-derives `leaf_w` from the opening's `area` in P3 and changes nothing while `area` is still 0** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: BLOCKING, the LEAF slot had no initial state at weld time, so a P2 reader between the weld and the P3 hook saw an open gap)*, rebuilds the grid; bumps `version` (and `static_version`, LY-12 d) of **every section whose socket state changed — the host section of `socket_a`/`socket_b` whether or not it moves — and of every moved section**, and marks the dirty keys of LY-32: `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<survivor>`, `BODY/<absorbed>`, and `SEC/<id>` for each of those sections. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier text bumped moved sections only, so the unmoved host's PLATE → JAMB + LEAF change was invisible to a version-keyed consumer.)* The bump reports REGION for the two socket-host sections and FRAME for the other moved sections (LY-12 d); `body_of` of every moved section changes in this apply (absorbed -> survivor) and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick; Emitter State derives its `body_id` from it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The mated hatch's opening ids are read from the Graph (`seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`, ordinal = the index in `socket_plan.openings[]`) into a derived cache `opening_leaves` (edge id → the leaf slots it drives, LY-11); the cache is not persisted and is rebuilt in `post_restore` (LY-26 d). **Host rule (deterministic, argument-order independent):** the surviving body is the body with the **lower `body_id`** (the older body; the home-ship, built first, in the MVP). `socket_a` and `socket_b` are re-labelled internally by survivor, not by argument order, so D.6's `offset_b = 

**LY-17 — Recording a cut; detach and body ids.** `detach_section(seam_id, boundary_mode)` (LM3, Class A) runs after the Graph's `cut_detach` (LSG:172). It marks the weld row `CUT_SEALED` or `CUT_RAGGED` with `cut_at_T`; sets both sockets `CAPPED` (SEALED) or `CUT_OPEN` (RAGGED); then runs connected components over the ACTIVE `welds[]` in ascending `section_id`. The component containing the body's `origin_section_id` keeps its `body_id`; the other component receives a NEW `body_id` from `next_body_id` (KRN:197: "Detach allocates a new body ID from the Layout block") and its `origin_section_id` is **`m`, the minimum `section_id` of that component** (D.12 — the same section whose origin becomes the new frame origin); its offsets are re-based so its frame origin is its minimum-id section's origin (D.12). **Dirty keys and versions (the rule of LY-12 d):** `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>`, and `SEC/<id>` plus a `version` and `static_version` bump for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the kept-side section even though it does not move) and every moved section**. If the hatch was open when it was cut (`area` > 0), the kept section's LEAF slot goes inactive and its PLATE goes active in the same apply, so the bump is what tells a version-keyed consumer that a light gap has become a solid plate. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The bump reports REGION for the two socket-host sections and FRAME for the other moved sections (LY-12 d); `body_of` of every moved section changes in this apply (kept/new split) and is readable by any ordered reader in the same tick; Emitter State derives its `body_id` from it *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* **Entombment: who owns the guarantee that no actor stands where the PLATE materialises** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the severity is RECOMMENDED because the crisis cut and lethal friendly fire make the state reachable and AC-28 treats such an overlap as a Body defect)*: **Layout performs no actor check** (it reads nothing from `body.state`, LY-18) and `apply` places the PLATE unconditionally. On the **CHANNEL cut path** the guarantee is Assembly's: the completion `validate` blocks the cut outright (`MSA.CUT_BLOCKED`, MSA-21) while any crewmate's foot box overlaps the open hatch passage, using `detach_preview`'s `rects[]` (the PLATE footprint) as the test region. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* There is no cut path around Assembly's completion `validate`: CHANNEL rejects with `MSA.CUT_BLOCKED` and CASCADE (the "crisis" cut) defers and is abandoned on ex

**LY-18 — Bodies, membership and the Body boundary.** Layout owns `bodies[]`, each `section_instances[].body_id`, offsets, and `welds[]`. Ship Body owns pose, velocity, actor positions, kinematics and any engine-side shapes built from Layout data. Body repeats *(Ship Body & Interior Physics is designed; BDY repeats this)*: its ownership of `body.state` (pose, velocity, actor positions); `restore_after: [layout.state]`; and the physics PROJECTOR (KRN:197, KRN:198). Layout reads nothing from `body.state` (acyclic). *Correction surfaced to the 2D Lighting stage:* its brief says "Ship Body owns frames and `body_id`"; the kernel's "Detach allocates a new body ID from the Layout block" (KRN:197) decides it — Layout allocates the id and owns membership; Body owns the frame's POSE. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**LY-19 — Discard.** `discard_section_geometry(section_id)` (LM4, Class A) runs after the Graph's `discard_section` M4, which requires no ACTIVE seam (LSG:172). Precondition: no `WELDED` socket, else `SECTION_WELDED`. It marks the instance row `discarded` (a **tombstone**: ids are retained so they are never reused — the Graph's LS-21 form), removes its rects from the grid, dissolves its sole body and bumps `version`. Weld-history rows that name the section stay (Pillar 5), and the surviving mate's socket keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` state. Items that lay in the section belong to Interaction and are carried or destroyed by the orchestrating apply (CR-9 atomicity), not by Layout.

**LY-20 — Hardpoints are Layout declarations; the Item DB decides what fits.** HARDPOINT fields per LY-4. The Graph's ABSENT or installed node is the runtime state; `compatible_defs(h)` (IDB F-6, IDB:577-594) is the Item DB's pure function, called by Layout's STRUCTURAL lint: every hardpoint has at least one compatible def; a LOAD (kind 13) hardpoint without `accepted_subtypes` is a lint ERROR (heater and lamp share a port signature) — this unblocks IDB AC-18 (IDB:1180). `socket_tag` is an advisory lint hint, never authoritative; port types are (IDB:169). A hardpoint's footprint rect (`MACHINE` flag, static) stays whether or not a module is installed: a pedestal or mount remains after salvage and Layout has no dependency on node state. The nouns stay distinct: **HARDPOINT** (module slot, node-backed) versus **LOOSE SLOT** (LY-22); the index's "salvage/module slots" means both.

**LY-21 — A HULL_SEGMENT has no hardpoint.** The hull plate is a PART, not a module (HULL_SEGMENT has no `def_id`, IDB-5, LSG:185). `plate_positions[]` per HULL_SEGMENT = the host wall-face tile set (the Graph's `tiles` field, LSG:68), `bound_room_key`, and `exposed` (true iff the run is HULL); `segment_at(face_tile) -> segment_key | NONE` is a read, and `plate_positions(section_id)` lists the records in ascending HULL_SEGMENT node id (template order). It is the input of Adaptive Audio's `hull_anchor` derivation (AA-17, registry `hull_anchor`: the floor-division centroid of the lowest-id HULL_SEGMENT's plate set composed with `section_offset`), which Layout confirms as the contract (CX-A4); Layout publishes no `hull_anchor` read, because Layout's geometry reads answer section-local by default (LY-3 c). The DESTROYED-segment replacement path (LSG:755 against M5's ABSENT/SALVAGED precondition, IDB Open Questions 1 and 11) stays routed to the Graph and Item DB owners (C-9); Layout states only the geometry. Precondition for the MVP slice's seven HULL_SEGMENTs (LSG:228): every room tagged `outer` has at least `HULL_RUNS_MIN` disjoint exterior wall runs **that bear a FACE (a `CAP_ONLY` run, including every HULL run on a room's south edge, D.14, has no face to carry a plate and is not counted)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, each long enough for a segment's face tiles, separated by `SEGMENT_GAP_MIN_PX` so two breach trails do not overlap at the wall base; plate positions of different segments never share a wall tile (lints `OUTER_ROOM_HULL_RUNS`, `SEGMENT_TILE_SHARED`).

**LY-22 — Loose slots and story slots; no item table.** LOOSE SLOT = `{slot_id, room_key, anchor_px, surface FLOOR|SHELF|CRATE, allowed_class[], capacity 1}`. The authored start placement `{def_id, count, condition_bp}` is Derelict Authoring's CONTENT, expanded to an ItemInstance by the Item DB's `fresh_instance` and placed by Interaction's `place_loose(inst, section_id, pos_px)` at world build *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Layout's schema reserves NO item table**: the loose-item holder is Interaction's `interaction.state` *(orchestrator ruling; Interaction is designed and IA-36 adds it)*, which adds `layout.state` to its own `restore_after`. One writer per fact (kernel H3): Interaction performs every instance move (IDB:426-452), and atomicity with a discard or detach is given by CR-9 whichever owner's mutator holds the rows. Layout supplies `loose_slots(section_id)`, `floor_tile_at(section_id, px) -> tile | NONE` (placement validity) and `body_of(section_id)`; an item position is `(section_id, pos_px section-local)`, so a weld or a detach moves nothing. STORY SLOT (Vertical Slice; art bible 6.5 ("one cause, one verb, one absence per wreck", placed as three tagged slots)) = `{slot_id, role CAUSE|VERB|ABSENCE, room_key, anchor_px}`; the list is reserved in schema v1, empty and lint-checked in MVP, so the Vertical Slice addition is not a `schema_version` bump. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**LY-23 — Anchors.** `anchor_geometry(anchor) -> {kind WALL_FACE|FLOOR, host_face_id, base_px_polyline[], sort_origin_y, section_id}` (FT:306 names verbatim). The Graph descriptor anchor `(node_id, port_local_index)` or `edge_id` (LSG:152-153, "Layout supplies the polyline") maps to a template anchor through `section_of(id)` and `graph_ref_base` (id minus base = template-local index). The polyline is axis-aligned, integer, wall part first then floor part (FT-13); `edge_len_px = Σ|Δ|` (D.8) and must not exceed `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` (1152, 24 tiles — the Failure & Trail knob's content bound, owned here as a lint: Layout REJECTS a longer polyline and never shortens it, FT:642). It returns nothing, without error, for an id whose section is DISCARDED (FT:703-704: the draw must not crash). `sort_origin_y` is per Pipeline D.12 for WALL_FACE and `NONE` for pure FLOOR anchors (floor marks are not Y-sorted). `subject_anchors(section_id) -> [{local_key, kind_hint DOOR_FACE|HARDPOINT|SOCKET|SLOT|CONSOLE|INSTRUMENT, anchor_px, room_id, console_role}]` where `console_role` is `POD` or `DOCK` and is present iff `kind_hint` is `CONSOLE` (a structural lint `CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET`, ERROR, rejects a CONSOLE anchor without a role and a role on any other kind); Layout asserts no placement: Derelict Authoring authors them (a POD anchor in every dock room, a DOCK anchor in the home airlock only; its lints `POD_CONSOLE_MISSING` and `DOCK_CONSOLE_MISSING`) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: two DOOR_FACE anchors per **interior** door, one per face, each `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` outside the leaf's occupied span (EM:208 e); **a socket hatch gets ONE inner-face DOOR_FACE per hatch per section, plus its WELD_SOCKET anchor** (the outer face lies in void or in the mate's wall, which would conflict with `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE` and `DOOR_APPROACH_CLEAR`, so no outer-face anchor is placed; the mate's own section carries its own inner-face anchor) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; "Layout places, Interaction names the kind and registers". Presentation rebuilds anchors statelessly from Layout on Layout's `SEC/<id>` and the Graph's `T`/`SEC/<id>` (FT:265, FT AC-107). A wall fitting with no floor-run record is a lint error (`WALL_FITTING_NO_RUN`, FT:703), not a hidden trail. Layout must not grow a "trail" field: Failure & Trail reads Graph descriptors only and has no block (FT:26).

**LY-24 — `V` and `exposed_tiles` never change while a room exists.** The MVP promise to the Graph, as rule text: "`V` and `exposed_tiles` of an instantiated room never change while the room exists" (LSG:840 is the Vertical Slice re-base rule, not an MVP path). `V` is D.3. `exposed_tiles(room)` is the sum of the lengths of the room's HULL wall-run segments (D.4), static at build; socket frames and plate positions lie inside HULL runs (lint) so they are counted once, and a weld does not change it. The **conservative error** this accepts: a welded, closed hatch still radiates as hull. It is quantified in Edge Cases (the single MVP socket is 2 of the fixture airlock's 6 exposed tiles, D.4; a larger outer room would carry 20-40) and the Vertical Slice re-base is routed to the Graph owner in Open Questions. The Graph's lint ranges (`V` 4-200, `exposed_tiles` 0-80, LSG:299, LSG:452) are the Graph's variable ranges (not reason codes); Layout's structural lint reports a room outside them under its own lint ids `V_RANGE` and `EXPOSED_RANGE` and restates no bound. *Which value governs (answers Derelict Authoring OQ-DA-13):* D.4 evaluated on the loaded template's HULL runs governs everywhere, including across a 24-px jog (each run's `len_tiles` counts once); an authoring design table is documentation, and Authoring's `EXPOSED_DRIFT` WARN (tolerance 1 tile) reports where the two differ.

#### 1.5 Construction, restore, mutators, reads

**LY-25 — World construction order.** `build_section(template_id, kind) -> {section_id, body_id}` (LM1, Class A) = allocate ids → record the instance on its own NEW body at `offset_px` (0, 0) (the body frame's origin is its minimum-id section's origin, D.12) → Graph M1 `instantiate_section(section_id, template_id, kind)` (the Graph's own table names the caller "Layout / derelict build, home-ship setup", LSG:180; `kind` is an argument forwarded to M1 and is **not persisted by Layout** — the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17, LSG:174) → store `graph_ref_base` → build the grid → bump `version`. **Every built section starts on its own body, and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (authored welds in Vertical Slice procgen use `attach_section` with `welded_at_T` 0): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the weld relation stays a forest (LY-14) and the component split of LY-17 stays exact. **Layout calls NO Emitter or Interaction mutator.** The orchestrating atomic apply — Web Map & Transit's `init_world(world_seed)` per Save/Load SL-18 (SL:255, run in `LOADING` in `restore_after` order under a WriteScope), the only caller of LM1 (the pod is built there once, as one persistent body, and a pod hop builds nothing — Web Map CF-LY; Assembly never discards (MSA-24) and is not an LM1 caller (C11)) — calls, inside one WriteScope and in this fixed order: Layout `build_section` → Emitter E1 `instantiate_section_emitters(section_id)` (its stated caller stays "Assembly / Web Map atomic apply", EM:147) → Interaction `sync_section(section_id)` → PROJECTOR notification *(Web Map & Transit and Interaction are designed; the call order is theirs to repeat)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Layout supplies their data through reads (`subject_anchors`, `loose_slots`, LY-22, LY-23). This keeps `restore_after: []` honest: Layout depends on nothing at restore. The MVP world (home-ship + derelict A + derelict B + the always-dormant pod: four sections on four bodies, registry `mvp_template_roster`) is a data file `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` consumed by `init_world`; the floor plans in it are Derelict Authoring's. The build is incremental and the PROJECTOR reports ready when its scene content exists; Transit's `ARRIVING` is the fixed-length state `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` 45 ticks; the Pipeline, not the sim, holds the bla

**LY-26 — Restore, the two validity classes, and template drift.**
(a) `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` validates into scratch (failures via `ctx.fault(LAYOUT_RESTORE_*)`), then replaces the block's contents in place (copy into the existing block object, never replace the object; root rule ADR-0003 section 2) and only on success *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*; an unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure (`ctx.fault`), never a silent default. The snapshot obeys SL-2 (SL:176): no `Vector2i`, `Rect2`, `Color` or `Resource`; integer vectors travel as two ints or a packed integer array; dictionary keys are String or int; 64-bit values (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`) never travel as JSON numbers (two 32-bit halves or strings remain legal; a native int64 is also accepted in the binary payload, exact; the convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON, i.e. the header and the dev dump-save) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Concrete encoding rules** (JSON text turns int keys into strings and numbers into floats; the payload itself is `var_to_bytes` binary, SL-2, but the dev `dump-save` JSON and the generic K-3 round-trip test must not change a table's meaning): (1) **no integer-keyed Dictionary** — every table (instances, sockets, welds, bodies) is a dense set of parallel packed arrays in ascending id order, so a stringified key can never be misread; the few Dictionaries are String-keyed and hold only scalars and packed arrays; (2) **64-bit values** (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`; and `layout_hash` wherever Save/Load's header carries it, which is not `layout.state`, D.10 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) travel as **two 32-bit int halves** `(hi, lo)` (or exact strings; a native int64 is also exact and legal in the binary payload, so this convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON: the header and the dev dump-save; ADR-0006) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*, each normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` before any compare (D.10) — the project convention (Interaction `last_salvage_T`, Assembly `last_shape_change_T`, and D.21's two-int count) — and are rendered as exact-width lowercase hex strings (`Hex64`) **only by Save/Load's header** (SL-2 S-1), never as a JSON number. The dev `dump-save` does **not** use hex: per ADR-0006 section 1.3 item 4 it renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a lowercase **decimal string**, and the t
(b) *Class 1 — static queries, valid immediately after `restore()` returns.* Every query that depends only on templates and the instance table — `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static `rects_in`, `section_offset`, `body_of` — is valid at once, because templates were loaded in BOOTING and the instance table is the only restored state. This makes the Graph's loud failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM` on mis-order, LSG:831) impossible by construction whatever the order of `post_restore` calls.
(c) *Class 2 — leaf-dependent results, valid only after Layout's own `post_restore()`.* DOOR_LEAF rects depend on the Graph's persisted `area`, which Layout cannot read inside its own `restore()` (the Graph restores after Layout) and which the Graph now publishes as `opening(edge_id) -> {area, area_max, door_state}` (LY-10; the ask is closed, OQ-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **(orchestrator ruling; routed amendment to the Layout-side promise "every query is valid immediately after restore":)** leaves are derived by one `derive_doors` pass in Layout's `post_restore` (the kernel guarantees every `restore()` has completed before any `post_restore()` begins, KRN:843, so the Graph's persisted `area` is in memory whatever the order of the `post_restore` calls) and thereafter by `layout.doors`. Between `restore()` and `post_restore()` leaf-dependent queries (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage` (reports `open_extent_px` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) report the TEMPLATE default (every leaf closed) and raise a `stale_leaf` diagnostic flag if read. **Self-heal:** Layout's `post_restore` bumps `version(section_id)` (1 → 2) for every section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed template default; LY-12(d)'s "a restore is an unconditional rebuild signal" and the Emitter's W0 `version` read (EM:227) therefore rebuild the Emitter's static layer on tick 1 with no ordering between the two `post_restore` calls, and `body.integrate after: layout.doors` (LY-10) covers every P3 reader. Whether `post_restore` order follows `restore_after` is **informational only** (CR-8 and KRN:843 say "after every `restore()`"); no Layout rule depends on the answer. The `stale_leaf` diagnostic and this restore path are **live behaviour**, not a stand-in for an unanswered ask: they stay as specified now that the Graph read exists, because the window between `restore()` and `post_restore()` is real whatever the Graph publishes. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `post_restore` also bumps `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each such section, and rebuilds the derived `opening_leaves` map from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`.
(d) `post_restore()` does cross-block VERIFICATION only: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves in the Item DB catalogue (a diagnostic, not a hard fail), and every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph SeamRecord. Failures use the restore reason set (LY-29).
(e) *Template drift.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The single `template_hash` is **split in two**, both persisted per instance (D.10): `geometry_hash` (u32; the canonical bytes of everything that decides where a rect, tile, socket, door or anchor is — room `origin_px` and tile runs, wall runs and the compiled rect table, socket `facing`/`line_px`/`start_px`/`width_tiles`/`hatch`, door positions and `area_max`, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines) and `visual_hash` (u32; kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels, hinted flags that no query reads). `restore` refuses an unknown `template_id` (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`) and a STRUCTURAL change (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`: the sets of `room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `node_ref`, or any room's tile set differ) **and a geometry change on an instance that carries history** — `geometry_hash` differs and the instance has any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or shares its body with another section — because a moved socket, wall edge or doorway under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment while every key set still matches (a socket position or wall rect edit used to classify as "visual-only"). A geometry change on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone is accepted with one diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh` (nothing depends on it yet and its rects are re-derived from the new template); a `visual_hash` difference alone is accepted with one diagnostic. Pre-release saves are disposable (SL-14, adopted verbatim); after the first build given outside the project the migration obligation of LY-6(e) applies. `rot_q` must be 0 (LY-3 d).

**LY-27 — Mutators.** Layout has four mutators, all Class A (command-backed, validate-then-apply, CR-9) and **no Class B** (clamp-never-reject): it holds no quantity that can sensibly be clamped. Each has a pure `can_*` validate query; `apply` is infallible once validated (a failure inside `apply` is a defect and sends the kernel to `FAULTED`).

| # | Mutator | Takes | Validate (pure) | Caller | Marks (dirty keys) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LM1 | `build_section` | `template_id, kind` (`kind` forwarded to M1 only, never persisted); returns `{section_id, body_id}` | `can_build`: template known, Layout capacity (`MAX_SECTIONS`, `MAX_BODIES`, rooms, rects, **`MAX_DOORS_LOADED`** (loaded doors plus the template's doors; *added 2026-10-27 — re-review: the edge case 'refused earlier by `can_build` with `CAPACITY`' had no validate clause behind it*), **`next_section_id <= 2^20 − 1`**, the bound D.9's `rect_key` needs *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), Graph `CAPACITY` pre-check | Web Map `init_world` (the only caller; a pod hop builds nothing) | `SEC/<id>`, `BODY/<id>` | Layout |

*(CLARIFY, adopted — deviation from the brief's provisional list.)* There is NO `install_cap_plate` and NO `set_socket_state` mutator: a socket's state changes only inside LM2/LM3, atomic with the Graph's weld and cut, so a cap plate or a scar cannot exist without its cut record and no caller can desync them. **Dirty tracking is explicit inside each mutator** — the Godot 4.7 packed-array element-write change (setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole property, breaking-changes 4.6→4.7; kernel CR-8 "4.7 gotcha") means a setter-based dirty flag would silently miss element writes, and `layout.state` is mostly packed arrays.

**LY-28 — Read views (the one true channel).** All reads are pure, side-effect free, deterministic, callable from `validate`, P3 and presentation, and **none has a "perceived" variant** (the mirror of LSG:199). Frame and ordering are part of the contract.

| Query | Returns | Frame | Order | Valid after | Owner of the fact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `room_at(section_id, px) -> room_id \| NONE` (sill px → `sill_room`) | id | section-local | n/a | `restore`; hook-callable (Suit SE-3) | Layout |

| `V(room_id)`, `exposed_tiles(room_id)` | ints | n/a | n/a | `restore` | Layout |
| `room_surface(compartment_id) -> {floor_tiles[], wall_faces[]}` | FT:306 shape | section-local | tile id ascending | `restore` | Layout |
| `room_boundary(room_id)` | polyline | section-local | clockwise from min tile | `restore` | Layout |

offset_a + pos_a − pos_b` always places the *absorbed* frame in the *survivor's* frame and `frame_shift_px` has one sign convention; a call with reversed arguments therefore produces the identical result, and the dissolved body is never the home-ship's by an argument mix-up. `welds[]` is **canonicalised**: it records the survivor-side section and socket as `section_a`/`socket_a` and the absorbed side as `section_b`/`socket_b` whatever the call order, so a reversed call produces a byte-identical block and `layout_hash`. Layout returns `{surviving_body_id, absorbed_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px}` (`frame_shift_px` as defined in D.6: the absorbed frame origin in the host frame, added to every moved section's offset) so Body can emit `BODY_TRANSFER` (PIPE:694) and keep the avatar's screen position where the layout allows — Body's concern. A weld **moves nothing already built** (the Graph's LS-15): only the absorbed body's frame is re-based, a translation of whole tiles. Layout records no `q` (Assembly's) and no cut mode until a cut (LY-17).
======
xpiry, never forced (MSA-21, MSA-22). As a net behind that, Body REFUSES (it does not eject; BDY-24 iii, ruled 2026-10-28, delegated ruling G6): `rebase_on_detach` takes this record's `rects[]` and returns `-BDY_REBASE_ACTOR_IN_CAP`, writing nothing, if a foot box overlaps them. Layout still performs no actor check. `detach_section` also checks `CAPACITY` in its validate (LY-29). Returns `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}`, where `rects[]` is exactly `detach_preview(seam_id).rects[]` (the seam's hatch rectangles, one per side, pre-cut body frame, computed before the sockets change) so prediction and apply cannot drift *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **A cut through a compartment is not representable:** a cut is requested only by `seam_id` (LSG:849 "Cuts happen only along seams, never through a compartment"), so Layout has no "cut here" geometry input. A cut never splits gas by a volume ratio because a compartment belongs to one section (LSG:172).

content.content:
**LY-31 — The PROJECTOR contract.** Layout's data module is scene-tree free (kernel H10): a headless test asserts it references no `Node`. A **separate PROJECTOR** (subscriber class `PROJECTOR`, CR-10: "write engine-side *derived* objects owned by its block owner … never writes blocks"; kernel example "Layout → physics projection; derelict content build") builds engine-side derived objects from `layout.state` and the templates (its scripts live in `src/presentation/projector/`, never in `src/sim/layout/`; ADR-0010 section 1.2) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*; they are never persisted and are rebuilt from the block, also after restore. The object shape (the [UNV] default and the weld spike that measures it) is in the engine feasibility note and ADR-LAY-03, not in this contract. It builds the door, prop and machinery sprites from the rect table and the seam bead, cap plate and scar pieces from `welds[]` and socket state. It fills the Pipeline's PR-5 layer stack (floor z 0 never Y-sorted, floor marks, ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding in tree order wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery, actors; wall caps) and gives every placed SPRITE object (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead or plate piece) the Pipeline's **`entity_id`** (PIPE D.12, PIPE:553: persistent, owned by the state block, stable across save and reload; the third key of `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, PIPE:1139). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `creation_id` is retired; the Pipeline has no such field.)* **Layout's `entity_id` (publisher-defined, G1; the namespace tag is registered with the Pipeline, Open Questions OQ-LY-ID):** a block-tagged int64, `entity_id = (LAYOUT_ID_NS << 56) | (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | template_local_idx`, with `LAYOUT_ID_NS` a Layout namespace byte in `1 … 127` (GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit, so a byte of 128 or more would make every Layout `entity_id` negative; the Pipeline compares ids as plain ints and only relative order inside one namespace matters, but the range is fixed so the sign is never in question) that Body, Interaction and any other id publisher must not use in its own high bits (so a Layout id can never equal a Body or Interaction id in the same `class_rank`), `section_id` 32 bits at most (`next_section_id` is monotonic and tombstones keep their ids), `kind_ordinal` 8 bits, `template_local_idx` 16 bits. It is a pure function of the block (`section_id`) and the template, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one, and it is never persisted by the PROJECTOR. **Tiles carry no `entity_id`:** `TileMapLayer` cells are not nodes; wall-face and cap tiles are `class_rank` 0 and tie-break among themselves by cell position `(y, x)` (the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`, Y-sort mechanism per SP-YSORT-1 below). Within `class_rank` 2 the doors, props and machinery of one `sort_y` are ordered by `entity_id` alone (they share one rank in the Pipeline; Layout assumes no sub-rank). The *mechanism* that delivers the key (`TileMapLayer` participation, who owns child insertion order) is not defined here and stays gated on SP-YSORT-1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* It writes no block and creates **no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in MVP**. It never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (Lighting's). Its section nodes are parented under Body's per-body root `Node2D` (Body's `body.projector` owns the root and its translation, BDY-33) — the default shape, which the Y-sort spike below may supersede with option B (no reparent; BDY-33 would then own the pose-driven section positi

**LY-32 — Dirty keys and notification.** Layout's batch `(layout.state, tick, change_keys)` carries `SEC/<section_id>`, `BODY/<body_id>`, `S/<seam_id>`, or `ALL` past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256. **Encoding** (registry: `layout_dirty_key_encoding`)**:** Layout's keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id` with KIND in {SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3} (the Graph's LS-20 encoding, LSG:201), written in this document by family name; the family name `S/<seam_id>` is the Graph's (LS-20) and Failure & Trail's (FT:264, FT AC-107), so `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` accounting is comparable across blocks. Dirty keys are namespaced by block (CR-10; KRN:465 bounds them per block), so Layout's `SEC/<id>` and the Graph's `SEC/<id>` (LSG:170) are different keys in different blocks; every subscriber names the block, and subscribers that need both (Failure & Trail anchors, FT AC-107) subscribe to both.

**LY-33 — Determinism, hashing, seam age.** `layout_hash` is the kernel's `block_hash` of `layout.state` (D.10, kernel D.12); the kernel's `state_hash` folds it unchanged and derived caches (`version`, grids, leaves) are excluded *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)*. **`layout_hash()` does not cover door state** (Horror C-HE-13): `area` and `door_state` are the Graph's and hash in `graph.state`, and the leaf rects are excluded derived caches; a reader caching on door geometry keys on `version(section_id)`, which `layout.doors` bumps whenever a leaf changes (LY-12 d). All iteration is over dense arrays in ascending id order, never a Dictionary. Layout draws no RNG in MVP (`rng_derive` unused). `welded_at_T` is the only time value stored. **Seam bead age is DERIVED, never a flag:** `age_class = OLD` iff `T − welded_at_T ≥ SEAM_OLD_AFTER_TICKS` (D.11); the 4-px Hull Grey bead (art bible 8.2), its straight/corner/T and fresh/old variants, and the cap plate are PRESENTATION pieces on the wall-mounted layer.

**LY-34 — Pillars as tests; no lie in geometry.** *P1 (primary):* one rectangle set for collision, light and drawing; no "perceived" variant of any query; a phantom door is the Perception Filter's presentation and is falsified by the rect. Layout carries no phantom-geometry field, no "false door" record, no sanity input and no per-player variant of any table; a flag named hallucinated, fake or perceived is struck on sight. **Granted (Perception Filter PF-5 row 11, grade TRUTH_ST; OQ-13 resolved):** wall faces, door leaves (ordinary doors and hatches alike) and socket/seam geometry are truth-channel — the Filter's rule, which Layout accepts; Layout's narrower fallback was recorded there, not adopted (OQ-PF-14). *P5:* seams and scars persist as geometry (LY-16, LY-17). *P3, P4:* indirect only. *P2:* no Layout mechanic. *Anti-pillars:* no runtime "place a wall / draw a room" capability exists; sections attach only at pre-declared sockets; no blueprint export or import (SL:120).

**LY-35 — Not owned (scope guard).** Layout does not own: `door_state`, opening `area`, VALVE `open`, breaker `closed`, atmosphere, node/edge state, failure (Graph); pose, velocity, `LocomotionStep`, the foot box (Body / Controller); the occlusion test, the cone test, `Light2D` / `LightOccluder2D`, shadow slots (Emitter / Lighting); weld/cut/install commands, `q`, the preview cursor (Assembly) and `can_join` (Graph); trail stamps, extents, dullness (Failure & Trail); the loose-item table (Interaction, LY-22); a `visited` or "explored" bit — `layout.state` is WORLD-scoped and rolls back on `request_restore` (CR-8, KRN:855), so a bit here would reset too; campaign-level "first entry" knowledge belongs to a PROFILE-scoped owner or Web Map & Transit's world model (Save/Load SL:825 names the alternative source), Layout supplies only the pure `room_at` and routes the owner question to Open Questions; the def vocabulary and the `compatible_defs` body (Item DB); the world list, seeds, deltas, loaded set (Web Map & Transit); authored floor plans and the room-kit art (Derelict Authoring, art-director); the camera and zoom (Pipeline); procgen grammar and ART 6.3 rules 1-8 (Procedural Derelict Generation, Authoring); sanity, hallucination and perceived values (none exist in Layout); UI (see UI Requirements). `door_passage` is derived door geometry (D.5), not door state: Layout still owns neither `area` nor `door_state` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*.

**Engine feasibility (Godot 4.7.2, GDScript).** *Default PROJECTOR shape [UNV] (→ ADR-LAY-03; the spike SP-YSORT-1 of LY-31 tests the no-reparent option B first, so read this default as the fallback, option A):* per-section `TileMapLayer` nodes parented under Body's per-body root `Node2D` (owned by Body's PROJECTOR `body.projector`, BDY-33; Layout's PROJECTOR creates the section nodes); one map per body is what the weld spike measures (batching and Y-sort under reparent are [UNV]). `docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui, and has **no `scripting.md`, `core.md`, `tilemap.md` or `2d.md`**: `TileMapLayer` behaviour (batching, Y-sort under reparent, rotation, collision), `var_to_bytes` determinism and GDScript packed-array cost are **NOT SOURCEABLE in the engine reference** and are tagged [UNV] where used. Knowledge gaps: **HIGH** — merged-versus-per-section `TileMapLayer` batching cost and Y-sort behaviour when sections are reparented under a moving body node (the 50-300-draw figure is NOT SOURCEABLE until the weld spike); **HIGH** — the Y-sort tie rule (tree order) [UNV], which is why the Pipeline's `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` key exists and Layout supplies a stable `entity_id` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: was `creation_id`)*; **MEDIUM** — `var_to_bytes` determinism and typed-container encoding of the snapshot dictionary [UNV] (SL-2); **MEDIUM** — `TileMapLayer` rotation, collision and navigation behaviour in 4.6/4.7 (Layout deliberately uses no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh, so this blocks only a later PROJECTOR-to-physics decision, which is Body's); **MEDIUM** — GDScript cost of `rects_in` over about 2,000 rects with a uniform grid against the Controller's 0.05 ms per actor per tick budget (spike). ### D.5 Door leaf and passage

The door leaf formula (registry: `door_leaf_gap`) is defined as:

`gap(area) = floor_div(width_px × area, area_max)` · `leaf_w(area) = width_px − gap(area)` · `passes(F) ⇔ gap(area) ≥ F` · `area_pass_min(F) = ceil_div(F × area_max, width_px)` · `leaf_would_overlap(opening, area′, boxes) = ∃ L ∈ leaves(opening), ∃ f ∈ boxes : overlap(leaf_rect(L, area′), f)` (*Amended 2026-10-27 — design review:* `leaves(opening)` is one leaf for an interior door and **both** leaves of a mated hatch, each at its section's body-frame offset, with the opening's single `area_max`)

where `leaf_rect` for a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w` is: hinge `LOW`: `[s, s + leaf_w) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; hinge `HIGH`: `[s + width_px − leaf_w, s + width_px) × [w, w + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes. The leaf slides INTO the pocket on the hinge side, so the visible leaf stays anchored to the hinge end of the doorway and the gap opens from the other end. `leaf_w = 0` returns no rect (its `idx` stays reserved, D.9).

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `width_px` | int (px) | 96 (the 96 × 96 door cell, art bible 8.2); lint `DOOR_WIDTH` | template | doorway width |
| `area` | int | `0 … area_max` | the Graph's opening state, read through `opening(edge_id)` (LY-10; published, the ask is closed); for a mated hatch, the shared OPENING's | the opening's current `area` (the Graph states 1/64 tile, LSG:72) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `area_max` | int | `> 0` (the one refusing bound: a named structural invariant, because D.5 divides by it); default 64; guidance range 32–128 (`A_HOLE_MAX` 64, range 32–128, LSG:323 — cited as the scale reference; a value outside 32–128 is not a boot error, is never clamped and appears only in the ADVISORY range report) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix: the earlier hard `≤ 128` ceiling is withdrawn; ADR-0007 § 2.5)* | template; for a mated hatch `min(a.area_max, b.area_max)` (LY-15) | full-open value; lint `DOOR_AREA_MAX` (refuses `area_max` ≤ 0 only) |
| `F` | int (px) | 16 across a doorway in an E-W wall, 8 across one in a N-S wall | the foot box 16 × 8 (PCI:103), supplied by Body | foot-box extent across the doorway |
| `hinge` | enum | `LOW`, `HIGH` | template (interior door); fixed `LOW` for a socket hatch (LY-9) | pocket side |
| `leaf_w`, `gap` | int (px) | `0 … width_px`; `gap` monotone non-decreasing in `area` | derived | leaf length and open length |

**Output Range:** `leaf_w`, `gap` in `[0, 96]`; the product `width_px × area` is at most `96 × 128 = 12,288` at the top of the guidance range (a larger `area_max` is legal and the product stays far inside the 64-bit `int`; `area` is clamped to `[0, area_max]`, so `leaf_w` stays in `[0, 96]` for every `area_max > 0`) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix)*. At `area = 0` the leaf covers the doorway; at `area = area_max` there is no rect. Because the formula has no threshold, a binary jump `0 ↔ area_max` is binary by consequence and `DOOR_LIGHT_OPEN_PM` is retired (LY-9).

**Example (`area_max` 64):** `area` 0 → `leaf_w` 96; 32 → 48; 64 → 0; 21 → `96 − floor_div(2016, 64) = 96 − 31 = 65`, `gap` 31; 10 → `gap` 15, 11 → `gap` 16. `area_pass_min(16) = ceil_div(1024, 96) = 11` (check: `gap(10) = 15 < 16`, `gap(11) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = ceil_div(512, 96) = 6` (`gap(5) = 7`, `gap(6) = 9`). With `area_max` 128: `area_pass_min(16) = 22` (`gap(21) = 15`, `gap(22) = 16`) and `area_pass_min(8) = 11`. Leaf rect of `door_cryo_s` (E-W wall footprint `y` in `[384, 408)`, doorway `x` in `[240, 336)`, hinge `LOW`/west, `area_max` 64) at `area` 32: `[240, 288) × [384, 408)`, gap `[288, 336)`. **Close-safety:** closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w = 96 − floor_div(1920, 64) = 66`, leaf `[240, 306) × [384, 408)`; a foot box `[296, 312) × [384, 392)` overlaps it (`240 < 312`, `296 < 306`, `384 < 392`, `384 < 408`), so `leaf_would_overlap` is true and a PLAYER-origin close returns `OBSTRUCTED` (LY-11). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Mated-hatch example (the seam-straddling case):** the `fixture_airlock` weld of D.6 with `area_max` 64 (the minimum of 64 and 128): the opening's leaves are A's `[672, 696) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)` and B's `[696, 720) × [240, 240 + leaf_w)`. Closing from `area` 32 to 20 gives `leaf_w` 66, so both leaves reach `y` 306. The foot box `[696, 712) × [296, 304)` overlaps **only B's leaf** (`696 < 720`, `296 < 306`; against A's leaf `696 < 696` is false), so `leaf_would_overlap(opening, 20, [box]

**Passage record (`door_passage`)** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: `orientation` = `EW` for a door in an E-W wall, `NS` in a N-S wall. For a doorway starting at `s` in an E-W wall whose footprint starts at `w`: `sill_rect = [s, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`; `open_extent_px = gap(area)` (0 when closed, 96 when `area = area_max`); `gap_rect`, hinge `LOW` = `[s + leaf_w, s + 96) × [w, w + 24)`, hinge `HIGH` = `[s, s + gap) × [w, w + 24)`; a N-S wall swaps the axes (`sill_rect = [w, w + 24) × [s, s + 96)`). `gap_rect` is NONE iff `open_extent_px = 0`, and equals `sill_rect` when `area = area_max`. The OUT convention is LY-12 (b)'s: every returned rect is the occupied span `(x0, y0, x1 − 1, y1 − 1)` (the half-open figures above are the stored form). The read returns NO passable flag: the caller compares `open_extent_px` with its foot extent `F` (`passes(F) ⇔ gap ≥ F`; `F` supplied by Body/Controller, PCI:103: 16 across an E-W doorway, 8 across a N-S one). **Mated hatch:** the opening's single `area_max = min(a, b)` and the fixed LOW hinge (LY-9, LY-15) apply; each section answers for its OWN leaf in its OWN section-local frame, and both answer the same `open_extent_px`. The read re-uses the leaf value `layout.doors` last projected (the same `leaf_w` that sizes the leaf rect), so collision, light and passage cannot disagree and `opening()` is not read a second time; an unknown opening reads as closed (the existing `opening_unknown` edge case), so `open_extent_px = 

**Worked values** (`door_cryo_s`, E-W, `s` 240, `w` 384, hinge LOW, `area_max` 64; `sill_rect` span (240, 384, 335, 407) in every row): `area` 0 → `open_extent_px` 0, `gap_rect` NONE; `area` 4 → `gap` floor_div(384, 64) = 6, LOW (330, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 245, 407); `area` 8 → 12, LOW (324, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 251, 407); `area` 11 → floor_div(1056, 64) = 16, LOW (320, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 255, 407); `area` 32 → 48, LOW (288, 384, 335, 407), HIGH (240, 384, 287, 407); `area` 64 → 96, `gap_rect` (240, 384, 335, 407). **N-S variant** (a harness-added door, as AC-52 adds `door_b`; `w` 384, `s` 240, footprint `x` in [384, 408), doorway `y` in [240, 336)): `sill_rect` span (384, 240, 407, 335); `area` 8 (12 px): LOW (384, 324, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 251); `area` 4 (6 px): LOW (384, 330, 407, 335), HIGH (384, 240, 407, 245). Against `F`: 6 px is passable across neither orientation, 12 px across N-S only (12 ≥ 8, 12 < 16), 16 px across both. `area_max` 128 with `area` 1 gives `open_extent_px = floor_div(96, 128) = 0`.

### D.6 Weld offset and the 24-grid closure

The weld offset formula (registry: `weld_offset`) is defined as:

`pos(socket) = (line_px, start_px)` for facing E or W, `(start_px, line_px)` for facing N or S · `offset_b = offset_a + pos_a − pos_b`, where **`a` is the survivor-side socket and `b` the absorbed-side socket, assigned by body (the body with the lower `body_id` survives, LY-16), never by argument order** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* · mate holds iff facings opposite ∧ `width_tiles` equal ∧ classes compatible ∧ lane multisets equal ∧ `¬overlap(rect_a, rect_b + offset_b − offset_a)` for every static-footprint pair (all static rects with all flags, each PLATE at its full footprint, plus room tile cells; LY-14) (`GEOM_OVERLAP`)

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset_a`, `offset_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid; `(0, 0)` at build (LY-25); may be negative after a detach re-base | the block | body-frame section origins |
| `pos_a`, `pos_b` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid (lint `GRID_24`); local `≥ 0` | template sockets | the socket reference point (LY-13) |
| `width_tiles` | int | 1 … 12 (`L_seam`, LSG:328 — cited) | template | equal for both sockets of a mate |

**Output Range:** `offset_b` on the 24-px grid. **`frame_shift_px` (attach)** `= offset_b − offset_b_old`, the position of the absorbed body's frame origin expressed in the host body's frame (`offset_b_old` is section b's offset inside its own body before the weld, `(0, 0)` for a freshly built single-section body, LY-25); every section of the absorbed body GAINS `frame_shift_px` (`new = old + frame_shift_px`). D.12's detach `frame_shift` has the same meaning mirrored (the position of the split-off body's new frame origin in the old frame; moved sections LOSE it), so one sentence serves Body for both. **24-grid closure (one line):** every input of the sum lies on the 24 grid (`GRID_24`-linted) and `offset_a` does by induction from `(0, 0)`, so `offset_b` does — a derived property, not an input constraint, and the reason `OFFSET_OFF_GRID` is unreachable and no socket phase is needed. After translation the two hull footprints abut: A facing E occupies `[line_a − 24, line_a)` in its normal axis and B facing W occupies `[line_b, line_b + 24)`, which lands at `[offset_a + line_a, offset_a + line_a + 24)`.

**Example:** home-ship airlock socket E-facing, `pos_a = (696, 240)`, `width_tiles` 2, `offset_a = (0, 0)`; derelict B socket W-facing, `pos_b = (120, 144)`, `width_tiles` 2: `offset_b = (0 + 696 − 120, 0 + 240 − 144) = (576, 96)` — 12 tiles by 2 tiles, on the 24 grid. B's W wall footprint local `[120, 144)` lands at body `[696, 720)`, abutting A's E wall `[672, 696)`; B's hatch local `y` `[144, 240)` lands at `[240, 336)`, in line with A's. `L_seam = 2`. For this attach `offset_b_old = (0, 0)`, so `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`: the absorbed body's section 3 moves from `(0, 0)` to `(576, 96)` in the host frame, which is the same vector D.12's cut example returns when that seam is cut again. **Reversed-argument example** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: calling `attach_section(sock_b_w, sock_airlock_e, …)` — derelict B's socket first — still survives body 1 (the lower id, the home-ship), absorbs body 3, and returns the same `offset_b = (576, 96)` and `frame_shift_px = (576, 96)`; the roles `a`/`b` of the formula are the home-ship socket and B's socket in both calls. **`GEOM_OVERLAP` negative example:** a B bumper rect local `[96, 120) × [144, 192)` lands at body `[672, 696) × [240, 288)` and overlaps A's E wall `[672, 696) × [240, 336)` (`672 < 696`, `672 < 696`, `240 < 336`, `240 < 288`), so the verdict is `GEOM_OVERLAP`. A socket `start_px` of 150 never reaches this formula: it fails `GRID_24` at load.

### D.7 Capacity lint

The capacity lint formula is defined as:

`capacity_error(n, cap) = n > cap` · `capacity_warn(n, cap) = n × 100 ≥ cap × (100 − warn_pct)` · `subject_ok = max_subject_id < 2^20`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | int | 0 … 8192 | template (`nodes_in_template`, `edges_in_template`) | counts a template contributes to the Graph |
| `cap` | int const | 4096 nodes, 8192 edges | registry (`MAX_GRAPH_NODES`, REG:1805, edges folded into its unit string) | the Graph's `CAPACITY` limit |
| `warn_pct` | int | 10 | the Graph's warn margin (LSG:787) — cited | WARN band below the cap |
| `max_subject_id` | int | `< 2^20 = 1,048,576` | the Graph, LS-9 (LSG:123; LSG:915) — cited | highest id a subject may carry |

**Output Range:** ERROR (`CAPACITY_NODES` / `CAPACITY_EDGES` / `SUBJECT_ID_RANGE`) above the cap, WARN inside the band. The Graph's 800-node MVP bound (LSG:915) is Authoring's CONTENT lint, WARN at most, and is not enforced here.

**Example:** nodes = 3,700: `3,700 × 100 = 370,000 ≥ 4,096 × 90 = 368,640` → WARN; nodes = 4,097 → ERROR. Edges = 7,400: `740,000 ≥ 8,192 × 90 = 737,280` → WARN. The home-ship template at about 40 nodes passes silently; at 801 nodes it draws only Authoring's content WARN.

### D.8 Anchor polyline length and head clearance

The anchor polyline and head-clearance formula is defined as:

`edge_len_px = Σ_i ( |x_{i+1} − x_i| + |y_{i+1} − y_i| )` over an axis-aligned polyline · `edge_len_px ≤ TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` · `clear_ok(anchor) ⇔ ∀ i : free(p_i, normal) ≥ head_clear_px`, with sample points `p_i` every 24 px of arc length along the floor run and `free(p, normal)` the length of the maximal interval through `p`, normal to the final run segment, that lies in `tiles ∪ sill` and outside every `SOLID` span

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| polyline points | int pairs (px) | section-local; axis-aligned only (`POLY_DIAGONAL`) | template anchor | wall part first, then floor part (LY-23) |
| `TRAIL_EDGE_MAX_PX` | int const | 1152 (range 480–1536; 24 tiles) | registry (REG:1995), confirmed as the content bound | longest polyline Layout accepts; a longer one is REJECTED, never shortened (FT:642) |
| `head_clear_px` | int (px) | 144 | Failure & Trail FT-37 (FT:211) — cited, not restated | head clearance at a sev-4-capable anchor |
| `free(p, normal)` | int (px) | `0 … 48 × SECTION_MAX_TILES` | derived | the interval reading, adopted over the centred reading (LY-8 d) |

**Output Range:** `edge_len_px ≥ 0`, lint pass/fail; `clear_ok` boolean per sev-4-capable anchor with the first failing sample index reported (`CORRIDOR_HEAD_NARROW`).

**Example:** `anc_cryo_coolant`, polyline `[(48, 240), (384, 240)]`: `edge_len_px = 336 + 0 = 336` — the value Failure & Trail assumed (FT:377), with the far wall 7 tiles from the anchor — well under 1152. Samples every 24 px of arc length at `x = 48, 72, …, 360` (**14 points**, `(360 − 48) / 24 + 1`); the final partial segment `[360, 384)` is not sampled because its end point `x = 384` lies inside the E wall's footprint `[384, 408)`, where `free = 0` (the earlier '15 points, 48 … 384' counted a sample inside the wall) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; the normal is N-S. For `x` in `[240, 336)` the heater footprint `[240, 336) × [96, 144)` occupies the north part, so `free = [144, 384) = 240`; elsewhere `free = [96, 384) = 288`; minimum 240 ≥ 144, pass. A 2-tile corridor (96 px) hosting a sev-4-capable anchor fails at its first sample; a 3-tile corridor (144) passes exactly. A 1,200-px polyline fails `TRAIL_EDGE_OVER_BOUND`.

### D.9 Rect key, canonical order, leaf index and broadphase cells

The rect key formula (registry: `rect_key_order`) is defined as:

static `idx` = rank of the rect in the template sorted by `(y0, x0, y1, x1, flags)`, dense from 0 · leaf `idx` = `N_static + door_declaration_index` · **socket variant `idx` = `N_static + N_doors + 2 × h + v`**, where `h` is the socket's ordinal among the template's **hatched** sockets in declaration order and `v` is 0 for PLATE and 1 for JAMB (a hatchless socket owns none; a hatch's LEAF is its door's leaf slot) · `rect_key(section_id, idx) = section_id × RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` · `rects_in` and `solid_in` return ascending `rect_key` · for a **half-open** query box `[ax0, ax1) × [ay0, ay1)`: `cx0 = floor_div(ax0, BROADPHASE_CELL_PX)`, `cx1 = floor_div(ax1 − 1, BROADPHASE_CELL_PX)` (likewise `cy`), `cells = (cx1 − cx0 + 1) × (cy1 − cy0 + 1)` · **empty-box guard:** if `ax1 <= ax0` or `ay1 <= ay0` the box is empty or inverted, it touches **zero cells**, the query returns nothing (the caller's `QueryBuffer` is cleared) and raises the diagnostic `query_box_empty` — without the guard an inverted box such as `ax1 = ax0 − 200` yields `cx1 < cx0` and a formula product that can be a large positive count (two negative factors) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; G5)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: variant slots added; the closed query box is retired in favour of the one half-open input convention of LY-12 b)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N_static` | int | 0 … `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` | derived at load | static rect count of a template; the leaf indices are appended after it in door declaration order |
| `door_declaration_index` | int | 0 … `MAX_DOORS_PER_SECTION` − 1 | template | order of the door in its template |
| `N_doors` | int | 0 … `MAX_DOORS_PER_SECTION` | template | number of door records (interior doors and hatch doors); each reserves one leaf slot *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `h` | int | 0 … `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION` − 1 | template | ordinal of a hatched socket; reserves two variant slots (PLATE `v` 0, JAMB `v` 1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `RECT_KEY_STRIDE` | int const | `MAX_RECTS_PER_SECTION` 4096 | this GDD | key stride; `idx < 4096`; lint `RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW` if `N_static + N_doors + 2 × N_hatched > 4096` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `section_id` | int | `1 … 2^20 − 1` (`can_build` returns `CAPACITY` when `next_section_id > 2^20 − 1`, LY-27) | the block | so `rect_key < 2^32`; the key column is 64-bit (LY-12 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` | int | 48 (24–96) | this GDD | uniform-grid cell edge; a rect is inserted in every cell its span overlaps |

**Output Range:** `rect_key` in `[0, 2^32)`, unique and stable across attach, detach, restore and animation (an attach renumbers nothing); a leaf with `leaf_w = 0`, an inactive variant slot and a zero-length variant slot keep their `idx` and their keys are skipped. Lint `RECT_INDEX_DENSE` checks the union of **static, leaf and variant** indices is exactly `0 … N−1`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Example:** `fixture_cryo_excerpt` static rects, sorted: idx 0 N wall `[24, 408) × [72, 96)`; idx 1 W wall `[24, 48) × [96, 384)`; idx 2 heater `[240, 336) × [96, 144)`; idx 3 E wall `[384, 408) × [96, 384)`; idx 4 S wall west `[24, 240) × [384, 408)`; idx 5 S wall east `[336, 408) × [384, 408)` — `N_static = 6`, so `door_cryo_s` has leaf `idx = 6`; in section 3 its `rect_key = 3 × 4096 + 6 = 12,294`. A half-open query box `[380, 400) × [100, 112)` gives `cx0 = 7`, `cx1 = floor_div(399, 48) = 8`, `cy0 = 2`, `cy1 = floor_div(111, 48) = 2`, so 2 cells; **at a cell edge** `[96, 144) × [0, 48)` touches exactly cell column 2 (`cx1 = floor_div(143, 48) = 2`) and `[96, 145) × [0, 48)` touches columns 2 and 3. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Socket slots (two fixtures):** `fixture_socket_w2` (an E-facing socket, `line_px` 696, `start_px` 240, `W` 2, on a run that is exactly the span, one hatch door) has `N_static` 0, `N_doors` 1, so LEAF `idx` 0, PLATE `idx` 1, JAMB `idx` 2 (zero-width, omitted in every state); `fixture_socket_w3` (the same socket with `W` 3 on the run `[672, 696) × [192, 432)`) has static rects `[672, 696) × [192, 240)` (`idx` 0, before the span) and `[672, 696) × [384, 432)` (`idx` 1, after it), so `N_static` 2, LEAF `idx` 2, PLATE `idx` 3 (`[672, 696) × [240, 384)`), JAMB `idx` 4 (`[672, 696) × [336, 384)`, 48 px). In section 3 the `fixture_socket_w3` PLATE key is `3 × 4096 + 3 = 12,291`. A 16 × 8 foot box moving 3 px per tick sweeps at most a 22 × 14 box (D.22), which touches at most 4 cells.

### D.10 Hash and canonical bytes

The layout hash formula is defined as:

`geometry_hash = low32( H64( canonical_geometry_bytes ) )` · `visual_hash = low32( H64( canonical_visual_bytes ) )` (the two halves of the former `template_hash`, LY-26 e; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) · `layout_hash = block_hash(&"layout.state") = H64( canonical_bytes( layout.state snapshot ) )` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)*. `canonical_bytes` is the kernel's prefix-free TLV form (kernel D.12); Layout owns the snapshot SHAPE only (the AC-130 allow-list, arrays in ascending id order, tombstones retained, derived caches `version`, grids, leaf cache, PROJECTOR objects and `mutation_count` excluded) and writes no byte encoder for the block. `layout_hash()` calls the kernel read `block_hash(&"layout.state", uncached = true)` (new, kernel request K-2), which exists in every build because Horror HE-25 keys its path cache on it in release. The two template-local byte strings `canonical_geometry_bytes` and `canonical_visual_bytes` (and only those) are `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` per field in a fixed documented order (ADR-LAY-06); they are never compared with a kernel value

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H64` | function | 64-bit | the kernel's H64 (kernel D.12 and Tuning Knobs `H64`/`mix64` row; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling X13 / R-17): the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 computed with Godot's `HashingContext`; native, no GDScript byte loop *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* | one hash for the whole project |
| `canonical_geometry_bytes` | bytes | template-sized | template | rooms by `room_key` with `origin_px` and tile runs, rects in D.9 order, socket and door positions, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines; strings as length-prefixed UTF-8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_visual_bytes` | bytes | small | template | kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_bytes( layout.state )` | bytes | tens of bytes to tens of KB | the kernel's TLV encoder (kernel D.12) over the block snapshot | counters, bodies, instances, sockets, welds; Layout supplies the snapshot shape only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* |
| `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` | u32 each | `[0, 2^32)` | persisted per instance | drift gate (LY-26 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| hash cadence | policy | n/a | this GDD | see Output Range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

**Output Range:** `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` are u32, `layout_hash` is u64 and travels as two int32 halves in the payload (hex only in Save/Load's header, SL-2 S-1); none is ever emitted as a JSON number. The kernel's `state_hash` (kernel D.12) consumes `layout_hash` unchanged. **Cadence** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the kernel's GDScript canonical-bytes encode of the block plus the native SHA-256 is not free (kernel D.12 'Cost': dominated by the encoder, not by H64; [UNV], spike SP-ENG-1 P5), so `layout_hash` is **never computed per tick**: it is computed (i) when Save/Load captures the block, (ii) once after `restore()`/`post_restore()` and compared with the value **stored by its owner, Save/Load's `block_state_hash` for `layout.state` in the slot header (SL-1 `blocks[]`, SL-16; optional: written in dev/test captures, absent from a release capture, in which case no comparison is made; Save/Load owns the stored copy and `layout.state` holds no `layout_hash` field, which is why the AC-130 allow-list has none)**; this value is the kernel's `block_hash` of the same block, so equality is exact (AC-181) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* (a mismatch is a diagnostic, not a restore reason, because the kernel owns `state_hash` verification), and (iii) in debug builds at the kernel's `state_hash` cadence; the Debug Overlay is not a caller: it reads the kernel's cached `block_hash(block_id, uncached = false)` at the diagnostics cadence and never triggers an owner hash (ADR-0005 sections 5.3 and 5.4) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0005 sync)*; the result is memoised on a block `mutation_count` bumped by LM1-LM4, so a repeat call with no mutation costs O(1). **`mutation_count` is a non-persisted, non-hashed derived cache** (it is in no LY-2 table, in no snapshot and in no canonical byte), **reset to 0 by `re

**Example:** the `counters` dictionary `{next_section_id, next_body_id, next_room_id}` encodes in the kernel TLV as 102 bytes = 9 (DICT header: 1 + 8) + 30 (`next_body_id`: key 1 + 8 + 12 = 21, INT 9) + 30 (`next_room_id`: 21 + 9) + 33 (`next_section_id`: key 1 + 8 + 15 = 24, INT 9) — entries sort by encoded key, which orders the u64 length first, so the two 12-character keys come first (`next_body_id` before `next_room_id`) and the 15-character key last; 119 bytes including its own parent key `counters` (1 + 8 + 8 = 17). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* A visual-only template edit changes `visual_hash` but not `geometry_hash` or any key set or tile set, so restore accepts it with one diagnostic. A socket `start_px` or wall-rect edit changes `geometry_hash` with every key set and tile set unchanged: on a welded or otherwise non-`FREE` instance restore refuses it (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`); on a never-welded `FREE` instance it is accepted with `geometry_changed_fresh`. A tile-set edit is refused by the key-set comparison, not by a hash — a 2^−32 collision therefore cannot hide a structural change. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

### D.11 Seam age

The seam age formula (registry: `seam_age_class`) is defined as:

`age_class = OLD ⇔ T − welded_at_T ≥ SEAM_OLD_AFTER_TICKS`, else `FRESH`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `T` | int (ticks) | 0 … 2^53 | `kernel.clock` | the simulation tick |
| `welded_at_T` | int (ticks) | persisted, never a JSON number | `welds[]` row (LM2) | the only time value Layout stores |
| `SEAM_OLD_AFTER_TICKS` | int (ticks) | 36,000 (10 min at `TICK_RATE` 60), range 3,600–216,000 | this GDD | FRESH → OLD threshold; sim ticks only (paused and dormant time do not count) |

**Output Range:** boolean; monotone in `T`; a restore rolls `T` and the rows back together (WORLD scope), so age never contradicts itself.

**Example:** weld at `T = 100,000`: at `T = 135,999` the bead is FRESH; at `T = 136,000` it is OLD.

### D.12 Detach re-base and components

The detach re-base formula (registry: `detach_rebase`) is defined as:

components of the ACTIVE `welds[]` forest minus the cut seam, enumerated in ascending `section_id` · `C_keep` = the component containing the body's `origin_section_id` (it keeps `body_id`) · `C_new` = the other component (it receives `body_id = next_body_id`, then `next_body_id += 1`) · `m = min(section_id) over C_new` · the new body's `origin_section_id = m` · `frame_shift = offset_old(m)` · `offset_new(s) = offset_old(s) − frame_shift` for `s ∈ C_new` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: `origin_section_id = m` was unstated)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `welds[]` ACTIVE rows | list | forest (LY-14: every weld merges two bodies) | the block | the weld relation over sections |
| `origin_section_id` | int | a section id in the body | `bodies[]` | the body's frame anchor |
| `offset_old(s)` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid, may be negative | the block | body-frame offset before the cut |
| `frame_shift` | int pair (px) | on the 24 grid | derived | returned so Body keeps the avatar's screen position (PIPE:694) — Body's concern |

**Output Range:** exactly two components (the forest argument); keep-side offsets unchanged; new offsets are differences of 24-grid values, so they stay on the 24 grid; dirty keys `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>` and `SEC/<id>` for **every section whose socket state changed (both sections of the seam, the unmoved kept-side one included) and every moved section**; each of those sections also gets its `version` and `static_version` bumped (LY-12 d). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The LM3 return list is `{new_body_id, moved_sections[], frame_shift_px, rects[]}` with `rects[]` exactly `detach_preview(seam_id).rects[]`, computed before the sockets change *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

**Example:** home ship section 1 at `(0, 0)` on body 1 (`origin_section_id` 1); derelict B section 3 at `(576, 96)` welded to 1; a wing section 4 at `(1056, 96)` welded to 3. Cutting seam (1, 3): components `{1}` and `{3, 4}`; `{3, 4}` gets a new body from `next_body_id`; `m = 3`, `frame_shift = (576, 96)`; new offsets section 3 `(0, 0)`, section 4 `(480, 0)`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Dirty keys: 2 `BODY` (kept body 1 and the new body) + 3 `SEC` (section 1, whose socket state changed although it did not move, and the moved sections 3 and 4) + 1 `S` = **6**, far under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256; the earlier count of 4 missed the kept body and the unmoved section 1, whose open leaf becomes a solid plate. The new body's `origin_section_id` is `m = 3`.

### D.13 World tile ceiling and rect budget

The world ceiling formula is defined as:

`world_tiles = Σ V(room)` over rooms of the loaded set · `ERROR ⇔ world_tiles > TILES_WORLD_MVP` · `WARN ⇔ world_tiles × 100 ≥ TILES_WORLD_MVP × WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT` · `rects(body) ≤ MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `V(room)` | int | 4 … 200 | D.3 | room volume |
| `TILES_WORLD_MVP` | int | 600 | Failure & Trail table data (FT:598) — a lint ceiling, not a Layout constant | world tile ceiling |
| `WORLD_TILES_WARN_PCT` | int (%) | 90 (80–95) | this GDD | WARN line (540) |
| `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` | int | 2,000 (1,000–4,000) | this GDD, sized to the Controller's performance criterion (PCI:1078) | rect budget of one body |

**Output Range:** lint verdicts `WORLD_TILES_NEAR_CEILING` (WARN) and `WORLD_TILES_OVER_CEILING` (ERROR); a build over the rect budget fails `can_build` with `CAPACITY`.

**Example (the registry's authored roster, `mvp_template_roster`; the earlier illustrative 502 is retired):** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `home_ship` `V` total 182 (5 rooms), `derelict_a` 118 (4 rooms), `derelict_b` 149 (5 rooms): the three ships total **449**, which is 74.8 % of 600; the always-dormant `pod_cabin` (`V` 4) makes **453** (75.5 %) if counted — the figure AC-100, AC-140 and the registry all use. Both pass, well below the 540 WARN line. Rects: about 250–400 unmerged across the three ship sections (the pod adds a handful) (planning estimate), the home-ship body about 90–150, against 2,000.
