### D.21 Block size estimate

The block size formula is defined as:

`bytes ≈ 4 × ( 13·I + 10·K + 4·S + 3·B + 3 )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the instance row is 13 ints, one more than before, because `template_hash` is split into `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash`)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `I` | int | 0 … live cap + tombstones | the block | instance rows (13 ints each; discarded rows stay as tombstones, LY-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `K` | int | `I − 1` at most per body | the block | weld rows (10 ints: ids, state, two 2-int times) |
| `S` | int | 0 … `8 × I` | the block | non-`FREE` socket rows (4 ints) |
| `B` | int | 1 … | the block | body rows incl. `DISSOLVED` (3 ints) |

**Output Range:** tens of bytes to tens of KB against `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` 32 MiB (REG:1915); excludes the template-id strings and the snapshot container overhead [UNV].

**Example:** MVP after the one weld (four sections on four bodies, the pod included; the absorbed body's `DISSOLVED` row still counts): `I = 4`, `K = 1`, `S = 2`, `B = 4` → `4 × (52 + 10 + 8 + 12 + 3) = 340` bytes. A long campaign with 24 live and 200 tombstoned sections, 200 weld rows, 400 socket rows and 208 bodies: `4 × (2,912 + 2,000 + 1,600 + 624 + 3) = 28,556` bytes (about 28 KB), still four orders of magnitude below the ceiling; `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` 65,536 raises a diagnostic long before. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

### D.22 Query cost model (planning arithmetic, not a rule)

The query cost model formula is defined as:

`cost(query) = t_call + cells × ( t_cell + rects_per_cell × t_dedup ) + t_merge(candidates) + candidates × t_test + N_dyn × t_bbox + t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the dynamic leaf / variant list is not in the grid, so every query scans it and merges its hits into the key-ordered output; the earlier model omitted both terms)* and `tests_per_actor_tick = cells(swept_box) × rects_per_cell + sweep_tests` · one `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept box `[px − 8 − v, px + 8 + v) × [py − v, py + 8 + v)` (half-open), `v = V_RUN`, then an analytic axis-separated sweep (never one query per 1-px step); the per-tick aggregate is `Σ over actors cost(solid_in) + Σ over Emitter and Lighting queries cost(rects_in)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier model counted AABB tests only and omitted the cell lookup, the de-duplication and merge of a rect that spans several cells, the call overhead, and every non-Body consumer.)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cells(swept_box)` | int | ≤ 4 at cell 48 | D.9 | grid cells touched |
| `rects_per_cell` | int | about 4 | planning estimate [UNV] | broadphase density |
| `sweep_tests` | int | about 16 | planning estimate [UNV] | analytic sweep against the candidate list |
| `N_dyn` | int | about 6 (MVP body; up to `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` 48 as a stress bound) | planning estimate [UNV] *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | length of the body's dynamic leaf / variant list scanned by every query (bounding-box test each) |
| `t_bbox` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | one bounding-box reject test per dynamic entry (same order as `t_test`) |
| `t_merge_dyn(N_hit)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × `N_hit`, `N_hit` about 0–2 | **[UNV]** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | inserting the dynamic hits into the key-ordered output |
| per-test cost `t_test` | µs | about 0.5–1.5 | **[UNV]**, NOT SOURCEABLE (no GDScript cost data in the engine reference) | one AABB test *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| call overhead `t_call` | µs | about 1–3 | **[UNV]** | one GDScript call, buffer `clear()` and the 64-bit key column writes *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| cell lookup `t_cell` | µs | about 0.5–1 | **[UNV]** | one grid-cell index computation and read *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| de-dup `t_dedup` | µs | about 0.3–0.8 | **[UNV]** | one generation-stamp check per candidate (a rect spanning k cells is met k times) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| merge `t_merge(c)` | µs | about 1 + 0.2 × c | **[UNV]** | ordering the candidates by `rect_key` (insertion into the sorted output) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| Emitter-sized query | box | 288 × 288 px (lamp radius `R_DRAW_MAX_PX` 144) → up to 7 × 7 = 49 cells at cell 48, about 100–200 candidate rects | planning estimate [UNV] | a `rects_in` call from the Emitter's static-layer rebuild or a segment test; amortised by the `static_version` cache (LY-12 d) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| actors per tick | int | 4 seats + the horror entities in range (about 6–8 in the MVP) | planning estimate | the aggregate-actor case *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

*(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Output Range:** about 32 tests plus the cell, de-dup, merge and call terms, about 0.028–0.072 ms per actor per tick from the static table (low: 1 + 6.8 + 4.2 + 16 = 28 µs; high: 3 + 16.8 + 4.2 + 48 = 72 µs, at 4 cells and 16 candidates), plus the dynamic terms at `N_dyn` 6 and `N_hit` 1 (3–9 µs scan plus 1.2 µs merge), so **about 0.033–0.082 ms, rounded to 0.03–0.08 ms** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the earlier '0.04 to 0.08' did not follow from the table)* — above the Controller's budget of 0.05 ms P99 over 2,000 rects (PCI:1078) at the pessimistic end, which is why the pass lines are spike measurements (group K), not rules; the aggregate for 8 actors is then 0.26–0.66 ms of the 16.6 ms frame (**AC-164's aggregate line of at most 0.6 ms is the budget; AC-136's 0.05 ms P99 per actor is the target**, and the pessimistic end of the model exceeds the line, which is why group K is a spike) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and an Emitter-sized query is about 0.1–0.3 ms, paid only on a `static_version` change. The model is planning only. **Fallback ladder (cheapest rung first, each a data-layout step):** (1) tune `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` (24/48/96); (2) replace the sort in `t_merge` with per-cell pre-sorted arrays and a generation-stamp de-dup; (3) cache results keyed by `(cell set, static_version)` for static consumers (the Emitter's static layer already is); (4) merge collinear abutting wall rects at load (fewer rects, same occupied cells); (5) only then a GDExtension or C# rung, which needs technical-director sign-off and is out of the project's GDScript-only stack until granted. The weld's `GEOM_OVERLAP` t

**Example:** a body of 3 sections, 200 rects, an actor mid-room: the swept box `[px − 11, px + 11) × [py − 3, py + 11)` touches 1–4 cells, about 16 candidate rects, about 32 tests in total.

   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)

assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:

Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)

   (has_expected_hash false: the K-4 compare is skipped and the outcome verdict is NONE; true: MATCH or MISMATCH, a diagnostic only)

**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).

**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).

content.content:
**3.1 One encoder, no owner byte writers** (resolves the LS-21 / D.12 conflict and the framing half of OQ-8). Canonical bytes are produced only by `CanonicalEncoder.encode(value)` over the payload an owner's `snapshot(ctx)` delivers through `ctx.put(payload)`, or over a content value (ADR-0007 inputs). An owner's GDD describes the *shape* of its payload (keys, value types, row order) and never a byte layout. Consequently:
- The Graph publishes no `[u32 tag][u32 len][bytes]` writer. Its `snapshot` payload is a `Dictionary` whose values are named `PackedInt64Array` / `PackedInt32Array` / `PackedByteArray` fields (and the `def_off` / `def_utf8` pair), and the kernel encodes it. The "fixed documented order" of LS-21 is replaced by **sorted key order** (§ 3.3): renaming a payload key changes the hash and therefore needs a `schema_version` bump. The raw-bytes cost the Graph wanted is kept: a packed array reaches the buffer by one `to_byte_array()` copy (P14: 0.002 ms for 96 KB), with no per-element loop.
- `canonical_bytes()` and `block_hash()` on an owner (TR-lsg-021, TR-emitter-038, TR-debug-033) become kernel-side reads: `canonical_encode(snapshot payload)` and the kernel's `block_hash(block_id)` (§ 5). An owner that wants to expose "its hash" forwards to the kernel read; it computes nothing.
- The Item DB's `ItemInstance` "canonical positional encoding with canonical zeros" (TR-itemdb-012) is a **payload-shape rule**: an instance is an `Array` of `int`s in a fixed positional order, every non-applicable field present as the canonical zero, so a holder block has one encoding per state. The encoder then writes each as `INT`. The byte bound in TR-itemdb-029 (96 bytes per instance) was derived from `var_to_bytes(inst.to_array())`, which is ADR-0002's size check and ADR-0006's storage form, not hash input; the TLV size of the same array is 9 bytes per int plus 9 for the array header (open question 6).
- Packed arrays in a snapshot payload are duplicates, never live references to block fields (P7; the ADR-0003 snapshot contract), so neither the encoder nor a worker that later holds the payload can race a write to the block.

**3.2 The type set is closed.** One tag byte, then a self-delimiting body, so no encoding is a prefix of another and the map from normalised values to bytes is injective (D.12; KRN-HASH-01). All counts and lengths are **u64 little-endian**. Integers are 8-byte little-endian two's complement.

| Tag | Type | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | NIL | none |
| `0x01` | BOOL | 1 byte, 0 or 1 |
| `0x02` | INT | 8 bytes, little-endian two's complement |
| `0x03` | FLOAT | 8 bytes, IEEE-754 binary64 bits, little-endian, after normalisation (§ 3.4) |
| `0x04` | STRING | u64 UTF-8 byte length, then the bytes; **a `StringName` encodes as the `STRING` of its text** |
| `0x05` | VECTOR2 | two normalised FLOAT bodies (16 bytes, no inner tags); components widen from `float32` to binary64 |
| `0x06` | VECTOR2I | two 8-byte little-endian ints (16 bytes, no inner tags) |
| `0x07` | ARRAY | u64 element count, then that many tagged values in order. Typed and untyped arrays encode identically. |
| `0x08` | DICT | u64 entry count, then `key, value` tagged pairs sorted by key (§ 3.3). Typed and untyped dictionaries encode identically. |
| `0x09` | PACKED | 1 element-type byte, u64 element count, then the elements as raw little-endian bytes |

Packed element-type bytes: `1` `PackedByteArray` (1 byte per element), `2` `PackedInt32Array` (4), `3` `PackedInt64Array` (8), `4` `PackedFloat32Array` (4), `5` `PackedFloat64Array` (8), `6` `PackedStringArray` (each element a u64 length plus UTF-8), `7` `PackedVector2Array` (two 4-byte floats per element). Any other `Variant` type (an `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `Color`, `Rect2i`, `Vector3`, a packed array not listed) is `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`. Adding a tag or a packed type changes the hash definition and needs a new `hash_algo` (§ 4.4). `bool` is never confused with `int`: they have separate tags.

**3.3 Dictionary key order** (resolves the key-order half of OQ-8; this deliberately replaces D.12's "sorted bytewise by the encoded key bytes"). A dictionary's keys are all `int` or all of the string family (`String` / `StringName`); a mixture is `ENC_MIXED_KEYS`, and any other key type is `ENC_KEY_TYPE` (CR-4 already requires one key type). The encoder sorts:
- **`int` keys** ascending by signed numeric value (`-5, 3, 10`).
- **String-family keys** ascending by code point of `String(key)`, which equals UTF-8 byte order (P12). `StringName` keys are converted to `String` before the sort; the `StringName` comparison is never used.
- After sorting, two keys that are equal as text would be `ENC_DUP_KEY`. The check is kept for defence in depth (a hand-built key list in a test) but **cannot trigger from a `Dictionary`**: the engine treats a `String` and a `StringName` key of equal text as one key (P22), so the "never both" shape rule of § 3.6 is vacuous for dictionaries and no `ENC_DUP_KEY` fixture can be built from one. § 6 tests instead that a payload built with `String` keys and the same payload built with `StringName` keys encode identically.

The reason for the change: the bytewise order of the *encoded* integer key puts `3, 10` before `-5` and orders strings by length first, because the encoded key begins with a little-endian length. That order is deterministic but meaningless, and the diff the G4 test prints ("the first differing `block_id` and key") reads naturally only in value order. Value order is also what `Array.sort()` gives with no custom comparator, so the encoder needs no byte-comparison helper (GDScript cannot order two `PackedByteArray`s). Both orders are equally injective, so the change costs nothing in collision safety, and no hash exists yet. `gdd_sync` item for the kernel GDD D.12 and KRN-HASH-01.

**3.4 Normalisation.** `FLOAT` and the components of `VECTOR2`: `f != f` (any NaN, whatever its payload) encodes as the bits `0x7FF8000000000000`; `f == 0.0` (both zeros) encodes as `0x0000000000000000`; everything else as its binary64 bits. These need explicit branches because `encode_double` preserves NaN payloads and the sign of zero (P11). `PackedFloat32Array`, `PackedFloat64Array` and `PackedVector2Array` are **not** normalised by the encoder: they reach the buffer as raw bytes, and a NaN payload or a negative zero inside one survives (P11). Therefore owners keep NaN and `-0.0` out of packed float state (their mutators normalise), and in strict mode (§ 3.5) the encoder scans every packed float array for a NaN or a negative-zero bit pattern and fails with `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL`. Floats in SIM blocks are in any case outside the contract (§ 1.2); this rule only makes the exception safe.

**3.5 Errors and strict mode.** `encode` returns a `PackedByteArray` and sets `error` (an `ENC_*` code) and `error_path` (a short text path such as `bodies/2/pos`, built only when an error occurs, never on the success path). On error the returned array is empty and the caller treats the block as unhashable: `block_hash` returns `ok = false` with `BLOCK_HASH_ENCODE_ERROR`; inside a capture it is the existing `CAPTURE_ERROR` fault (ADR-0003 domain 0, code 7) with `error` and `error_path` in the detail. No new domain-0 fault code is added by this ADR. Codes: `ENC_OK` 0, `ENC_UNSUPPORTED_TYPE` 1, `ENC_MIXED_KEYS` 2, `ENC_KEY_TYPE` 3, `ENC_DUP_KEY` 4 (defence only, § 3.3), `ENC_DEPTH` 5 (nesting deeper than `ENC_MAX_DEPTH` 16, which also stops a cyclic container), `ENC_SIZE` 6 (output above `ENC_MAX_BYTES`, default 16 MiB, never below Save/Load's `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`), `ENC_FLOAT_IN_BLOCK` 7 (strict only), `ENC_FLOAT_NONCANONICAL` 8 (strict only). **Strict mode** is on in tests and `STRICT_DEBUG` builds and for content hashes (`Hash64.of_value`); it additionally rejects any `FLOAT` / `VECTOR2` / packed float in a block not on the float allow-list (§ 1.2). Release builds run the non-strict encoder on the capture and K-4 paths: correctness there rests on the owners' mutators and the tests, and a payload float would still encode canonically (normalised) rather than silently.

**3.6 Shape rules for payloads** (so the encoder stays cheap). A block of more than about 250 scalar fields snapshots as packed arrays, not nested dictionaries (D.11's per-block budget). Payload dictionaries use `StringName` or `String` keys (or `int` keys for per-id tables), never both (the engine merges the two string forms into one key anyway, P22). Derived caches, diagnostics counters (`graph_*`, `hash_invocations`, `horror.view.debug`) and anything marked non-persisted are not in the payload and never in a hash (TR-lsg-039, TR-horror-020). Entity references are stable ids, never array positions of a different block. The encoder walks the payload once; it allocates one scratch `PackedByteArray` that it reuses across calls, one `keys()` array per dictionary node, and the final exactly-sized result; that allocation belongs to the dirty path and is bounded by the number of dirty blocks (S0-e measures it). **Scratch and aliasing rules (P7).** `encode` returns a fresh, exactly-sized array (`slice` or `duplicate`); the reused scratch buffer is never returned, stored or handed to another thread. `PackedByteArray.encode_s64`, `encode_u32` and `encode_double` raise an error rather than growing the buffer when the offset is out of range, so the scratch is preallocated (or `resize`d) to the bound before each walk; `HashingContext.update` takes no length argument, so the scratch is `resize`d or `slice`d to its true length before every `update` (S0-e records whether shrinking keeps capacity: UNVERIFIED). Any array handed to the Save/Load worker (§ 5.6 ladder step 2) is a `duplicate()` owned by the job.

**3.7 Worked vectors** (the first four rows follow D.12's hand-derived examples; every row was produced by the GDScript probe, and the independent Python implementation reproduced the `INT 1`, `FLOAT 1.0` and `[[1],[2,3]]` rows, so the rest are still to be cross-checked in S0; `u64(n)` is 8 little-endian bytes and `s64(n)` is the same for a signed value; the `H64` column is the numeric value of the first 8 digest bytes read little-endian).

| Value | Canonical bytes | `H64` |
|---|---|---|
| `INT 1` | `02 u64(1)` | `0xA8514B868B9B6F67` |
| `FLOAT 1.0` | `03 00 00 00 00 00 00 F0 3F` | `0xF9257072CFA72232` |

**4.6 Content hashes** (inputs fixed by ADR-0007 § 3.4 and § 3.5). `Hash64.of_value(value)` = `H64(CanonicalEncoder.encode(value, strict = true))`. `catalogue_hash` = `of_value(rows)` where `rows` is an `Array` of per-def `Array`s of post-cast integers and `def_id` strings, sorted ascending by `def_id` in code-point order (equal to the byte order ADR-0007 requires). `template_hash`, `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash` = `of_value` of the post-cast template payload (or its geometry / visual sub-payload, whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's), computed once at load. Layout stores the `u32` form `Hash64.low32(h)` in a `PackedInt32Array` and compares only after `& 0xFFFFFFFF` (P9, TR-section-032). Content hashes are diagnostic and never gate a load (ADR-0007 § 3.4). Their golden vectors are committed after this ADR is Accepted (ADR-0007 Validation).

**4.7 What the kernel hashes and when.** No hash runs in P2 or P3, and none runs on a tick where no consumer asks (§ 5.4). The consumers are: the Overlay cadence (`DIAG_HASH_CADENCE_TICKS` 60, outside P3, cached profile); `layout_hash()` and Horror's path cache (`block_hash` read from P3 onward or a boundary, memoised by the caller on its own mutation counter); the snapshot capture (`SAVING`, uncached, one `snapshot` per block whose payload feeds both the canonical encode and Save/Load's `var_to_bytes`); the K-4 reproduction compare after `post_restore` (uncached); the `STRICT_DEBUG` tripwire (D.12: at most two whole-set uncached hashes per dispatch batch plus one around P5); and the tests. **Capture hand-off.** `request_snapshot()` returns `void` and the outcome arrives through the outcome handler (ADR-0002); the snapshot `ControlOutcome` carries `T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, `hash_algo`, `block_ids`, `schema_versions`, `block_state_hashes` and `enc_lens` for every persist block (WORLD and PROFILE; PROFILE blocks are hashed per block though excluded from PERSIST), all computed uncached in `SAVING`. ADR-0006 § 1.8 triggers PROFILE writes by comparing those uncached `block_state_hashes`.

**4.8 64-bit interchange** (TR-cmd-038, shared with ADR-0006). A value that can exceed `2^53` (`T`, `world_seed`, `state_hash`, every block hash, `campaign_id`) crosses a JSON boundary only as `hex64`; a `Marshalls.raw_to_base64` string is allowed for opaque byte blobs. A snapshot's in-memory round trip through `var_to_bytes` / `bytes_to_var` is lossless for `int64` (the binary form carries 8 bytes), and that is Save/Load's storage form; it is never hash input (registry `payload_size_check`). The Web Map's 8-byte seeds are `PackedByteArray` bytes in their block and so need no integer treatment (WM-37). **Every JSON-sourced number is a `float` on parse (P21)**, so even small ints arrive as floats and `str()` can print `5.0`; above `2^53` the parse loses bits silently. Header and content readers therefore cast through the ADR-0007 `IntField.read` / the `Hex64.decode` path only, reject non-integral or `> 2^53` values, and never pass a parsed `Variant` into a block; a boundary that skipped the cast would hand the encoder a `FLOAT` (`ENC_FLOAT_IN_BLOCK` in strict mode). ADR-0006's header decode is the first consumer.

content.content:
### 2. Versioning and migration

**2.1 Two levels, as SL-14.** `format_version` (container) is migrated by Save/Load; `schema_version` (per block) is migrated only by the owner inside `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` as a chain of registered pure functions `(old Dictionary) -> new Dictionary`. Save/Load never rewrites block data. `min_reader_version` equals `format_version` on every write in the MVP. A migrated payload is **not written back** to the old file; the next autosave writes the new shape, so a downgrade-then-upgrade cannot half-migrate a file.

**2.2 The block contract in ADR-0003 terms.** Reconciling SL-15 with the registered owner-callable contract (ADR-0003 § 1, registry `owner_callable_contract`): a persisted block registers `snapshot`, `restore`, `default_state` and `post_restore` as `Callable`s each returning `ctx.complete()`, with `supported_versions`, `persist_scope` and `restore_after` in its `BlockDescriptor`.

- `snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload: Dictionary)`: a deep copy (no aliasing of live state, so the encode may later leave the main thread; packed arrays in the payload are duplicates, never live references, ADR-0003 snapshot contract), plain data per § 1.2, rows sorted by id, no derived caches, no object references, transient fields normalised (TR-pc-020).
- `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version: int, ctx)` is **two-phase: decode and validate into scratch, then copy the contents into the existing block object**. This is the single wording of the rule; "whole-block replace" and "swaps whole tables from scratch" in owner GDDs mean *replace the block's contents*, never the object (registry `block_as_resource_or_node`; ADR-0003 § 2: read-view facades are long-lived).
- **Failure is reported through `ctx.fault(<OWNER>_RESTORE_*)`** with the owner's domain code and a named detail, never by return value and never by clamping; the kernel fires `load_failed` and Save/Load maps it to the `RESTORE_FAILED` class of SL-11. Owner GDDs that describe `(ok, reason, detail)` mean this (ADR-0003 sync, not this ADR's to change).
- `post_restore(ctx)` rebuilds derived caches and cross-block verification; `default_state(ctx)` fills a block missing from an older file whose `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`.
- A restore is idempotent: `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical except for the closed `REBASE_BLOCKS` list (SL-12), and the Graph's, Body's and Controller's tests prove it.

**2.3 Block versions are data, cross-checked at boot.** `added_in_format`, `RETIRED_BLOCKS` and the mandatory flag live in one committed file `assets/data/saveload/block_versions.json` (loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline in the composition root as a closed-schema table and injected, with the Save/Load `ScalarTable`, into `SaveService.setup()` as plain data, so `save` needs no import edge to `data`; `save` may type variables with ADR-0007's published value types, TD-27), not in `BlockDescriptor`, so ADR-0003's descriptor field list is unchanged. After the registry freeze, the composition root runs `SaveBootCheck.verify(block_versions, registry_view)`: a mandatory-derivation mismatch, a registered block that is also retired (`SL_BOOT_RETIRED_BUT_REGISTERED`), or a missing entry fails boot with a domain-1 `SL_BOOT_*` code and the root never starts the kernel. A persisted WORLD block is **mandatory iff its `added_in_format` is at most the file's `format_version`**; the MVP set in SL-25 is the *result* of that rule, not a hand-kept list.

**2.4 `registry_epoch` and `catalogue_version`.** `registry_epoch` (the header field that tells "the registry moved" from corruption) is the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text of the sorted lines `block_id:schema_version:added_in_format\n` for every persisted block, as lowercase hex. It uses `HashingContext` directly, **not** H64 or the canonical encoding, so it depends on neither ADR-0005 nor the kernel. A file whose `registry_epoch` differs from the running build's and fails a mandatory-set or schema step is INCOMPATIBLE-dev: never CORRUPT, never quarantined (SL-11, T-5 steps 18 and 21). `catalogue_version` is the Item DB's single integer offered by ADR-0007 § 3.4; it is written in the header as an `int`, and its only gating use is the newer-than-build refusal of § 1.10.

**2.5 `hash_algo` and `codec`.** `hash_algo` 2 names H64 (the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 via `HashingContext`, read little-endian, ratified by the GDD, owned by ADR-0005); 0 and 1 are reserved, never written (they are `hash_algo` ids, not hash values: no `H64` value is reserved as a sentinel, ADR-0005). An unsupported `hash_algo` skips the reproduction compare (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`, REBASED cause 4) so a kernel hash change is never a save-breaking event. `codec` 0 only.

**2.6 Policy and fixtures (SL-14, unchanged).** The migration machinery exists from format 1. Two goldens: `tests/fixtures/saves/v1-standin/` (regenerated freely until the registry settles) and `tests/fixtures/saves/v1/` (generated from the real registry at the first outside build, immutable, with a CI schema-drift fingerprint: the `registry_epoch` of the committed shapes may change only together with a `schema_version` or `format_version` bump). The obligation to migrate begins with the first build given to anyone outside the project; before it, a mismatched development save is refused as "made by an incompatible development build". This is the same moment ADR-0007's id ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`; one project-level decision flips both.

## Summary
Over a hundred requirements from seventeen GDDs (the 65 rows of `tr-baseline.md`, the TR-saveload-028 to 042 gap rows and the cross-system rows the traceability matrix assigns here) need a save file that is self-verifying, written without ever endangering a good generation, versioned from the first build, and paired with a per-slot `restore_epoch` that re-keys threat draws on death without letting quit or death be a reroll oracle. This ADR fixes one container (8-byte magic, JSON header, `var_to_bytes` block payloads, SHA-256 trailer), a ring of three generations written by one `Thread` per job that the main thread only polls, a two-level version scheme (container migrated by Save/Load, blocks by their owners), a reserved PROFILE side file in the same container (built at the first PROFILE block, not at MVP), and a `restore_epoch` held in two alternating checksummed files that is made durable before every `request_restore`. The service is a tree-free `RefCounted` in `src/save/`; a thin `SaveHost` node in `src/game/` polls it once per frame and owns the window-close interception. Settings persistence is out of scope.

content.content:
- **Magic.** `53 59 4E 53 45 41 1A` (`"SYNSEA"` and a SUB/EOF byte, so a text-mode tool stops early), then the container-layout id byte (`01` for `FORMAT_VERSION` 1). The file extension is `.sav`.
- **Streamed hashing, scoped.** Save/Load's own `HashingContext` (`HASH_SHA256`) use is limited to `payload_sha256`, the trailer and `registry_epoch`, fed in chunks (`update`) so no hash needs a second whole-file copy; **`update` is never called with a zero-length chunk** (it errors), so an empty payload or header is skipped. `state_hash` and every `block_state_hash` are computed by the **kernel, uncached, during the `SAVING` capture** (ADR-0005 §§ 4.7, 5.4) and arrive in the snapshot outcome; Save/Load never computes or re-derives an `H64`. Container byte layout (`encode_u32` for `header_len`, `slot_epoch` bytes) and integrity hashing in `src/save/` use the byte writers that ADR-0005 § 1.7 row 8 forbids in the kernel, sim and block owners; `src/save/` is exempt because that output never feeds `H64` or `state_hash` (TD-12). Reading a candidate checks `FileAccess.get_length()` against `MAX_SAVE_BYTES` first, then reads. Whole-file reads use `get_buffer` loops or `FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes`; both are acceptable, the length cap comes first.
- **One payload form.** Every block payload is `var_to_bytes(dictionary)` of the owner's plain-data snapshot **Dictionary**; that every persisted block `put`s a Dictionary is a Save/Load-side precondition checked by the type walk (the decoded root of each block must be a `Dictionary`), not a change to ADR-0003's `put(payload: Variant)` signature. **Canonical bytes are produced by the kernel (ADR-0005 § 3.1) and never stored:** the Graph's snapshot payload is a Dictionary of named packed arrays; storage is `var_to_bytes`; hash input is ADR-0005's TLV of the same payload. The GDD's second form ("the owner's own canonical byte form as raw bytes", SL-2) is **dropped as a container form**. Reason: one decode path, one type walk, and a restore hand-off that is always a `Dictionary`, matching ADR-0003's `restore(data: Dictionary, stored_version, ctx)` (no `form` field and no byte-blob hand-off shape to invent). State equality is `state_hash`, never file bytes (probed: insertion order changes the bytes).
- **Header** is the closed list of SL-1 plus the additions of § 2 (`catalogue_version` is already there). The per-block hash field is named `block_state_hash` (SL-16) throughout, beside `enc_len`; the header `state_hash` is the kernel's `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` from the capture outcome. `seats` is an array of `PlayerId` ints (MVP `[1]`: single-player is host peer 1 → PlayerId 1, ADR-0002 § 3, kernel CR-7; corrected 2026-10-29 from `[0]`): non-empty, unique, in range, covering every PER_PLAYER key; no peer id, binding table or controlled-entity table is stored, and the kernel rebuilds bindings after a restore (TR-saveload-037). `created_unix` is written from the `WallClock` port and is display metadata only. Unknown extra keys are ignored when `min_reader_version` is satisfied; a missing required key refuses.

**1.2 Interchange and the trust model (corrects SL-2).**

1. **The encoder does not refuse objects (probed).** `var_to_bytes` silently encodes an `Object` as an `EncodedObjectAsID` and `bytes_to_var` returns it. SL-2's wording "the form that does not encode objects" is wrong in the direction that matters: a stray object in a `snapshot()` would reach disk. The defence is therefore **not** the encoder. It is (a) the type walk, which rejects `TYPE_OBJECT` explicitly (an `EncodedObjectAsID` is an Object), and (b) the write-side `VERIFYING` stage, which decodes and walks the bytes the worker just wrote (T-4), so an object-bearing snapshot is caught at write (`SL_WRITE_UNENCODABLE`, previous generations intact) and never first at a death.
2. **Decode with `bytes_to_var` only.** `var_to_bytes_with_objects` and `bytes_to_var_with_objects` are forbidden outright, as are `Resource`, `.tres`, `.res` and `ResourceLoader` for any save path. `bytes_to_var` of hostile input returns `null` and logs an engine `ERROR` that code cannot suppress (probed): so the decode runs only **after** the trailer, the block table and `payload_sha256` have passed, and a `null` result for a block that must be a `Dictionary` is `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_DECODE_FAILED`. A forged file with correct hashes can still produce engine error lines; that is a tamper case, accepted, and the fuzz suite is told (Risks, ADR-0010 assumption).
3. **Allowed types, enforced by the walk, not the encoder (probed: `Vector2i` round-trips, so the ban is policy).** `null`, `bool`, `int` (full 64 bits, § 1.3), finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` with `String` or `int` keys, and the packed arrays `PackedByteArray`, `PackedInt32Array`, `PackedInt64Array`. Forbidden: `Vector2i` and every vector or rect, `Color`, `Object`, `Callable`, `Signal`, `RID`, `NodePath`, `StringName` as a key or a value (a `StringName` is decoded as one, probed, so it must be rejected, not coerced; ADR-0003's `StringName` block ids and the in-memory staged payload keys of § 3.6 are memory-only and never enter a file, where block ids are header `String`s), and non-finite floats. Typed `Array[T]` and `Dictionary[K, V]` **round-trip their values** through the encoder (probed; type preservation is not asserted), which settles SL-2's "untyped until the spike" note: snapshots may use typed or untyped containers; the walk checks the decoded element types either way. Bounds: `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH` 16, `MAX_DECODE_NODES` **provisional 100 000** (the GDD knob is 250 000; typical saves are 10 000 to 30 000 nodes and the bound stays lowered until the walk timing of SAVE-WRK-1 f is measured, then is raised only as far as that timing allows; a packed array counts as one node, unchanged), per `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` and `MAX_SAVE_BYTES`. Owners' `restore()` still validates meaning; the walk validates only type and size.
4. **JSON appears only in the header and in the dev-only `dump-save`.** A dump renders any `int` whose magnitude is at or above 2^53 as a lowercase decimal string and any `PackedByteArray` as `Marshalls.raw_to_base64`; it is diagnostics, never a load path (TR-lsg-022).
5. **No compression** in the MVP (`codec` 0; 1 reserved). A size alarm at `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES` 2 MiB is diagnostics only.
6. **Roots and staging.** The decoded root of every block must be a `Dictionary`, and the in-memory staged payload of § 3.6 is built from those. `Dictionary.make_read_only()` on a staged payload is **shallow** (probe 14): it is a convenience, never a guarantee, and owners must still copy what they keep. A deep read-only snapshot, where an owner wants one, is built by the owner from `duplicate(true)` at capture.

## System Layer Map

### The layering rule

The systems index orders systems by dependency (Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish). The architecture layers below are **responsibility** layers. One test decides the side: **a system that registers a SIM state block or a step hook is simulation; a system that registers none and only subscribes to the kernel is presentation.** Static content that is loaded once and never changes at runtime is data. The kernel and Save/Load are foundation because everything else registers with them.

The simulation side never reads the presentation side. Presentation reads committed simulation state through read views and writes only engine-side nodes. The one presentation class that may change the simulation is `INPUT_SURFACE`, and it does so only by submitting commands.

### Which way dependencies may point

The stack is a responsibility stack, not a rule that dependencies only point down. The rules are:

1. **Simulation to simulation, any direction.** Inside the simulation (Core and Feature), a module may call another module's read view or published mutator in either direction, as long as the step-hook graph the kernel topo-sorts stays acyclic. Examples that exist today: the Controller Sim (Core) reads Suit's `locomotion_cap` (Feature); Layout and the Graph call each other (`instantiate_section` one way, room identity the other). A consumer cannot finish before its provider exists or is stubbed, so these edges are sprint-ordering facts.
2. **No compile-time cycles.** Cross-system references go through `class_name` and typed interface base classes at the seams. `preload` of a sibling system's script is forbidden (a `preload` cycle fails to parse) and lint-checked (ADR-0010).
3. **Foundation host services read Feature state only through the kernel.** Save/Load polls owner read views (Assembly `last_shape_change_T`, Interaction `last_salvage_T`, the Attention view, Suit vitals) obtained through the kernel registry, never by importing those modules. The Pipeline root reads `body.state` the same way.
4. **Simulation never reads presentation.** One existing case breaks this: the Emitter reads the Failure & Trail glow table (`GLOW_BASE_PM`, `SEV_GLOW_PM`), which Failure & Trail owns. The table is static data, so it moves to Content data under ADR-0007; Failure & Trail still authors the values (IC-12). Presentation reads simulation only through read views and notifications.

### Layer assignments

| # | System | Layer | Side | Owns (exclusively) | Why this layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Command & Simulation Layer | Foundation | Kernel | `kernel.clock`, command queue, registries, binding tables, command log, kernel state, diagnostics | Every simulation system registers with it; it owns no domain state (H1). |
| 25 | Save/Load & Versioned Format | Foundation | Host service | Files under `user://saves/`, `campaign.json`, `slot_epoch_a.bin` / `slot_epoch_b.bin` (the pair), `profile.sav` (deferred to the first PROFILE block, not before Alpha); **zero blocks, zero hooks** | It serialises what the kernel snapshots; it cannot roll back with the world. |
| 3 | Item & Module Database | Foundation (data) | Static data | Immutable `ItemCatalog` built at boot; `ItemInstance` value type | No block, command or hook; every system reads definitions from it. |
| 14 | Derelict Authoring (Handmade Kits) | Foundation (data) | Content + lint | Section/world JSON, content lint table, placement records | Owns no runtime API (DA-1); produces data the Layout, Graph and Emitter load. |
| 4 | Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera | Foundation (presentation) | Presentation root | Viewport sizes, scales k and H, layer stack, `CameraSolver`, `present_time`, `world_to_hud` | Every visual system draws inside the frame it owns. |
| 2 | Life-Support Graph | Core | SIM | `graph.state`; hooks `graph.propagate.power/.atmo/.failure` | The truth of O₂, heat, power, coolant, fuel and integrity. |
| 11 | Ship Section & Layout Data Model | Core | SIM | `layout.state`; hook `layout.doors`; immutable templates | Single owner of geometry, sockets, rooms and ids. |
| 12 | Ship Body & Interior Physics | Core | SIM | `body.state`; hook `body.integrate`; `LocomotionStep` | Ship-local integer kinematics for every actor. |
| 5 | Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query | Core | SIM | `emitter.state`; hook `emitter.place` | Light as a simulation input that no hallucination can touch. |
| 7 | Player Controller & Input | Core (Controller Sim) + Presentation (Adapter, Presenter) | Split | `controller.state` (PER_PLAYER); hooks `controller.step`, `controller.noise` | The Controller Sim is world model; the Adapter and Presenter are presentation. |
| 8 | Interaction System | Feature | SIM | `interaction.state`; hook `interaction.step`; most verb commands | The verb layer and act-only-on-lit rule. |
| 10 | Suit & Equipment | Feature | SIM | `suit.state` (PER_PLAYER); hook `suit.vitals`; `equip_tool` | Personal survival state. |
| 13 | Modular Ship Assembly | Feature | SIM | `assembly.state`; hook `assembly.step`; five commands | The atomic weld/cut/install transaction. |
| 16 | Web Map & Transit | Feature | SIM | `web.state`; hook `transit.step`; pod commands; `init_world` | World model and the abstracted pod hop. |
| 17 | Attention System | Feature | SIM | `attention.state`; hook `attention.step`; `push_stimulus` | The web's attention and the breach state machine. |
| 18 | Horror Entities | Feature | SIM | `horror.state`; hook `horror.step` | One MVP behaviour. |
| 19 | Sanity & Hallucination Rules | Feature | SIM (+PERCEPTION_OUT) | `sanity.state`, `sanity.ledger`, `sanity.perception`; hook `sanity.drift` | Authoritative sanity; writes the only perception block. |
| 15 | Boarding & Salvage | Feature (design rules) | none | Design-time rules only (BS-1) | Realised by Interaction, Suit, Assembly and Web Map; no code module. |
| 20 | Perception Filter | Presentation | Query service | `perceived()`, decoy lists, truth-channel tags; no block (PF-1) | The only path from a true value to a corruptible display. |
| 6 | 2D Lighting & Occlusion | Presentation | PRESENTATION + PROJECTOR duty | Light2D/occluder node pools; modifier chain | Draws emitters; owns no simulation fact. |
| 9 | Failure & Trail System | Presentation | PRESENTATION, pure reader | `TrailSpec` resolver, trail nodes | Truth channel; immune to the Filter. |
| 21 | HUD & Suit Layer | Presentation | PRESENTATION | HUD node surfaces, `HudLayout`, `HudModel` | Reads Suit through the Filter. |
| 22 | In-World Instruments & Inspect View | Presentation | PRESENTATION | `InstrumentPresenter` per instrument | Where class (b) lies are drawn. |
| 23 | Chart Table (Web Map & Menus) | Presentation | PRESENTATION + INPUT_SURFACE | `ChartPick`, `PauseGate`, `SettingsStore` | Never lies; submits commands through the Adapter path. |
| 24 | Adaptive Audio & Tells | Presentation | PRESENTATION | Bus tree, voice pool, `cue_requests()` | Reads Graph, Attention, Horror state directly so audio can lead visuals. |
| 26 | Debug Overlay (True Values) | Presentation (tooling) | DIAGNOSTIC | Overlay model/view, observer log | Dev and playtest builds only. |

### Engine awareness: Foundation and Core

- **Kernel**: relies on `Node._process` ordering by `process_priority` and on `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` (LOW, but unverified for cross-node order, spike KRN-LAT-02); typed callables returning a `CompletionToken` (HIGH, 4.7 typed-return override rule); packed arrays with explicit dirty marking (HIGH, 4.7). *Reference: `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 → 4.7, GDScript rows.*
- **Save/Load**: `FileAccess.store_*` returns `bool` since 4.4 (MEDIUM; every return is checked); `DirAccess.rename` atomicity on Windows is unverified (LOW, flagged [UNV]). *Reference: `breaking-changes.md` § 4.3 → 4.4.*
- **Render Pipeline**: SubViewport stretch wiring, the 4.7 stretch defaults for new projects, D3D12 default on Windows, HDR output (HIGH). *Reference: `modules/rendering.md`, `modules/ui.md`, `current-best-practices.md` § UI and Input (4.7).*
- **Graph, Layout, Body, Emitter**: scene-tree free and integer-only, so no rendering or physics API risk. The shared HIGH risk is the 4.7 packed-array element-write change; all four mark dirty keys inside mutators. *Reference: `current-best-practices.md` § GDScript (4.7).*
- **Player Controller**: 4.7 device IDs (HIGH). *Reference: `modules/input.md` § 4.7 Changes.*

---

## Module Ownership

Ownership tables give, per module: what it **owns** (sole writer), what it **exposes** (others may read or call), what it **consumes**, and the **engine APIs** it calls directly. Names are exactly as in the GDDs; the GDD is the authority on signatures.

| Save/Load (`src/save/`) | Save files, `campaign.json`, `slot_epoch_a/b.bin`, `profile.sav`, worker job | Host-local reads `save_status`, `fail_escalated`, `SaveInfo`, `restore_reason`, `quit_held`, `quit_write_active`; calls `new_game`, Save & Quit, Continue, `cancel_held_close` | Kernel control plane, `state_hash`, snapshot payloads; owner reads for gates (`controller.state` loco_state, `attention.view`, Suit vitals, Assembly `last_shape_change_T`/`ragged_breach_open`, Interaction `last_salvage_T`, Web events) | `FileAccess` (MEDIUM: bool returns), `DirAccess.rename` (LOW [UNV]), `Thread` (LOW), `HashingContext`, `JSON` with depth bound, `Marshalls` |

**3.1 The choice.** A seam that is injected and that tests must double is an **`@abstract` base class, a "port"**, living in the `ports/` directory of the lowest layer that every consumer of the contract may import (the lowest layer that every consumer may import: `src/kernel/ports/` for `Clock`, which `src/sim`, `src/presentation` and `src/game` all reach; `src/sim/layout/ports/` for `OccluderSource`). Implementations `extends` the port; test doubles `extends` the port. A port is `RefCounted`, holds only `@abstract` methods, constants and (rarely) a documented non-abstract default; it holds no fields. The consumer types its `setup()` parameter as the port. A port with a single consumer may sit beside it (`src/save/wall_clock.gd`, the `WallClock` port of § 4.5); such files are listed as `port_files` in `modules.json` so `ARCH-05` still checks them.

Probed on 4.7.2 (P4): a subclass that omits an abstract method fails at parse time, which is the strongest guarantee available without a custom tool; direct construction of the port fails at parse time. The reflective `GDScript.new()` bypass is accepted: no game code constructs through reflection. If LINT-SPIKE-1(a) finds `Script.is_abstract()` (believed 4.5, UNVERIFIED), the E3 tier asserts it for every script under a `ports/` directory and for every `port_files` entry, closing the `ARCH-05` "ports are `@abstract`" check at the engine level instead of lexically.

**3.2 What it does not replace.**
- **ADR-0003 §1 stands.** Kernel-invoked owner callables (`validate`, `apply`, `hook`, `snapshot`, `restore`, ...) remain registered `Callable`s ending `return ctx.complete()`. That choice rested on many callables per owner, no inheritance coupling and stubs that register plain callables, not only on `@abstract` being unexercised. There is no `BlockOwner` port.
- **Ports are for injected collaborators**, not for owner callables and not for block contents: `Clock`, `ContentSource`, `SolidQuery`, `OccluderSource`, `WorkCounter`, `DiagnosticsSink`, `ObserverSink`, `WallClock`, and the stub points of TR-pc-045 and TR-charttable-038.

342:### 7. The missed-mark audit and the touch serial
### 7. The missed-mark audit and the touch serial

The architecture calls for "a debug-build check that every changed block marked a dirty key". A literal check is wrong for blocks whose GDD forbids a key per write: the Graph fires a key only when a quantum bucket changes (LS-20), the Emitter's pose never dirties (EM-26), Web Map marks zero keys per tick during a leg (WM-2). So the audit is built on two separate facts.

**The touch serial (always on, also in release).** The kernel keeps `touch_serial[block]`, a `PackedInt64Array` of `MAX_BLOCKS`, written only by a granted `open_for`. Every successful `scope.open_for(block)` stores the scope's serial into the block's slot (one store; the serial is a kernel counter incremented at each scope arming, so it also advances for same-`T` paused cycles). Because every mutator begins with `open_for` (ADR-0003), "this block may have changed" is derived by the kernel without the owner's help and is independent of whether the owner marked a presentation key. The kernel exposes it as `Kernel.touch_serial(block_index)`. **ADR-0005 § 5.2 adopts it** as the validity input of the per-block hash cache (`BlockHashCache`), because a dirty key cannot serve: a quantised Graph write that crosses no bucket changes the hash and marks no key. A dirty key can therefore never gate caching (ADR-0005 § 5.4: capture is always uncached). The serial is a registry member under the H1 allow-list (registries group, ADR-0003 amendment).

**The audit (runs wherever `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` runs).** It is gated on the injected `KernelProfile`, not on build names: it runs in the `STRICT_DEBUG` profile and in the test profile, exactly where the tripwire runs (kernel GDD CR-19(e), ADR-0003 § 7). Whether a playtest export carries `STRICT_DEBUG` is **UNVERIFIED** (an export-profile decision, Open Question 9). It reuses the per-block hash the tripwire already takes around P5; it adds no hash pass. It reads the tripwire's **kernel-internal uncached results**, `block_hash_any(block_index) -> int` (ADR-0005 § 5.3, which resolves its OQ-11), not the public `block_hash` API: the public call refuses a block the active scope has opened (`BLOCK_HASH_IN_WRITE`) and a `persist == false` block, which are exactly the blocks the audit needs after P4. A sweep compares each audited block with its previous sweep and applies one rule:

> **`MISSED_DIRTY_MARK`**: the block's hash changed since the previous sweep, `touch_serial` advanced (the block was opened), **no key was marked and no `ALL` was set** in that interval, and the block's key space has `quiet_writes_allowed == false`.

- A block that changed with the serial **not** advanced is a write outside a scope or a leaked mutable reference; that is the existing `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` and is not duplicated here.
- A key marked for an unchanged value is not a violation (marked, not diffed).
- **Cadence.** In unit, integration and CI soak tests with small worlds the sweep runs **every tick** (`AUDIT_EVERY_TICK`); under `STRICT_DEBUG` it runs at the tripwire's `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` (60) and within `TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` (1.0), so there it is a sample, not a proof. A bool guards the whole path; release exports pay one branch per tick.
- **Quiet blocks** (`quiet_writes_allowed == true`) are not audited by the hash rule, because it cannot distinguish a forgotten bucket-crossing mark from a legal sub-quantum write. **The list is illustrative; each owner's `KeySpaceDescriptor` plus the per-owner key-space CI test is the normative source.** Illustratively: Graph, Emitter, Body, Suit, Controller, Sanity, `web.state` (Web Map marks zero keys per tick during a leg, WM-2; it is quiet unless the Web Map ADR guarantees that no write happens without a key during a leg, otherwise a leg-progress write would raise `MISSED_DIRTY_MARK` on every sweep), and any block with a continuous family. `attention.state` is flagged for ADR-0022 to decide (TR-attention-026: presentation polls it every frame, and it may write without keys). For quiet blocks the guarantee is the per-mutator test of Implementation Guidelines (a fixture runs each mutator in a fresh kernel and asserts that its discrete changes mark a declared kind), plus a per-block diagnostics counter `QUIET_WRITE_TICKS` (ticks on which the block was touched with zero keys), shown in the Debug Overlay so a block that never marks anything is visible.
- **Scope of coverage.** `block_hash_any` hashes every touched block, including `persist == false` derived blocks, so those are audited too (when they are not quiet).

- **Release.** Nothing detects a missed mark at run time in a release export; the consequence is a stale display until the next full reconcile (Lighting LO-3 reconciles every `FULL_RECONCILE_TICKS` 60). This is accepted and recorded.

# Godot — Breaking Changes

Last verified: 2026-10-17 (4.6 → 4.7 and the section dates); 2026-02-12 (older sections)

Changes between Godot versions, focused on post-LLM-cutoff changes (4.4+).

## 4.6 → 4.7 (Jun 2026 — POST-CUTOFF, HIGH RISK)

From the official migration guide
(https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/migrating/upgrading_to_godot_4.7.html,
checked 2026-10-17). Rows marked **GDScript breaks** stop existing GDScript from
working; the rest add optional parameters, change C# compatibility only, or
change behaviour or defaults. The guide lists no deprecations.

| Subsystem | Change | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| GDScript | Overrides inherit a typed return | An override of a method with a typed return now inherits that type, so it needs an explicit `return` (add `return null` to fix the error). **GDScript breaks** |
| GDScript | Packed array element writes | Setting one element of a packed array no longer calls the setter of the whole packed-array property |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.ImageUpdateMask.UPDATE_WIDTH_IN_PERCENT` renamed | Now `UPDATE_WIDTH_UNIT`. **GDScript breaks** |
| GUI | `RichTextLabel.add_image()` / `update_image()` | `width` / `height` are `float` (were `int`); `width_in_percent` / `height_in_percent` renamed `width_unit` / `height_unit`, typed `RichTextLabel.ImageUnit` (were `bool`, default `false` → `0`). C# source breaks |
| GUI | `Control.accessibility_live` type | `AccessibilityServer.AccessibilityLiveMode` (was `DisplayServer.AccessibilityLiveMode`). C# breaks |
| Core | `Object.is_class()` | Parameter is `StringName` (was `String`) |
| Core | `OptimizedTranslation.generate()` | Returns `bool` (was `void`). C# binary breaks |
| Input | Mouse and keyboard device IDs | Were `0`; now `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` and `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, because some joypads use `0`. Identify events by type or compare `InputEvent.device` to those constants |
| Physics | Jolt: `WorldBoundaryShape3D` plane sign | The sign of `plane.d` is read the way Godot Physics reads it, so it is flipped compared to 4.6: negate it to keep 4.6 behaviour |
| Physics | Jolt: `SoftBody3D` mass and stiffness | Mass defaults to 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point); `linear_stiffness` is applied differently. Re-tune `linear_stiffness` and `damping_coefficient` on every `SoftBody3D` |
| Physics | Jolt: `Area3D` and `SoftBody3D` | `Area3D` now reports overlaps with `SoftBody3D`; use collision layers and masks to ignore them |
| Physics | `PhysicsServer2D.body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` | Optional `direction` added; `PhysicsServer2DExtension._body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision()` requires it (extensions break) |
| Audio | `AudioStreamPlayer2D` / `AudioStreamPlayer3D` `area_mask` default | Changed from layer `1` to `0` (disabled). An `Area2D`/`Area3D` `audio_bus_override` that relied on the default mask stops working until the mask is set back to layer `1` |
| Audio | `AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer.tap_back_pos` | Removed. **GDScript breaks** where it is used |
| Rendering | `CanvasItem` line drawing | No antialiasing feather is added, so lines look thinner; widen lines that relied on the old thickness |
| Rendering | `LinearToSRGB` visual shader node | No longer clamps to `[0.0, 1.0]` under Forward+ and Mobile |
| Rendering | `get_format()` moved | From `ImageTexture` / `PortableCompressedTexture2D` to base class `Texture2D` |
| Rendering | `RenderingServer.particles_request_process_time()` | `time` renamed `process_time`; optional `process_time_residual` added (also on `request_particles_process()` of the four particle nodes) |
| Rendering | Sky reflection roughness layers | `rendering/reflections/sky_reflections/roughness_layers` default `7` → `8` |
| Animation | `Animation.length` | Type metadata `double` (was `float`). C# breaks |
| Animation | `LookAtModifier3D.relative` | Default `false` (was `true`) |
| Animation | `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D.add_blend_point()` | Optional `name` added |
| Project | Stretch defaults for NEW projects | `display/window/stretch/mode` `canvas_items` (was `disabled`), `display/window/stretch/aspect` `expand` (was `keep`). Existing projects keep their settings |
| Text | `ResourceImporterDynamicFont.hinting` | Default `3` (was `1`) |
  ```

- **Script backtracing**: Detailed call stacks available even in Release builds

## GDScript (4.7)

- **An override of a typed method inherits its return type**, so it needs an
  explicit `return` statement; the migration guide's fix is `return null`
- **Writing one element of a packed array no longer calls the property's
  setter.** A setter on a `PackedInt32Array` (etc.) property no longer runs on
  `arr[i] = v`; assign the whole array where the setter has to run

## Physics (4.7)

- **Jolt `WorldBoundaryShape3D`**: the sign of `plane.d` now matches Godot
  Physics, flipped from 4.6. Negate it in scenes authored on 4.6
- **Jolt `SoftBody3D`**: mass is 1 kg for the whole body (was 1 kg per point)
  and `linear_stiffness` is applied differently; re-tune `linear_stiffness`
  and `damping_coefficient`. `Area3D` now reports `SoftBody3D` overlaps
- **Audio areas**: `area_mask` on `AudioStreamPlayer2D`/`3D` defaults to `0`
  (was layer `1`); set it to layer `1` where `audio_bus_override` areas are used

## Physics (4.6)

# ADR-0013: Ship Layout Block, Geometry and ID Allocation

## Status
Proposed

## Date
2026-10-29

## Last Verified
2026-10-29 (against `design/gdd/ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` LY-1 to LY-35 and D.5, D.6, D.9, D.10, D.12, D.21; ADR-0001 to ADR-0010, all Proposed; the engine facts marked "probed 2026-10-29" were run on the 4.7.2 mono console binary)

## Decision Makers
Claude (author), running under modes.automation: autonomous (project.yaml); decisions logged for the user's review; the user has not yet reviewed this ADR.

## Summary
Ship Section & Layout is the one owner of rooms, rectangles, sockets, welds, bodies and three id spaces, and every Core and Feature system reads or calls it, but no document fixes how its block is shaped, how its rectangles are keyed, how a weld moves a body or which side of the Layout/Graph boundary allocates which id. This ADR decides: `layout.state` stores **instances by reference** to immutable catalog templates as **dense per-column packed arrays** (rows addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones kept, a third persisted `structure_hash` added to the GDD's two); geometry is **integer half-open rectangles** with a flags byte in a reserved, never-renumbered `idx` space; sockets are **sparse terminal-state rows** changed only inside two mutators; weld offsets are computed on the **lower-`body_id` survivor** with a canonicalised `welds[]`; and ids are **split** so that Layout allocates `section_id`, `body_id` and `room_id` from persisted counters while the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids and Layout only stores the per-instance bases.

## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (pinned 4.7; installed 4.7.2.stable.mono, `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`) |
| **Domain** | Core (simulation data model; scene-tree free, integer-only; the PROJECTOR that draws it is ADR-0034's) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. The module uses no rendering, physics or scene API. The two HIGH items it touches are the 4.7 packed-array element-write change (every dirty mark here is explicit inside a mutator) and the 4.7 typed-return override rule (it applies to the `@abstract` port of § 8; the rule is sourced from `breaking-changes.md` § 4.6 to 4.7) |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows, 4.3 `TileMapLayer` row); `deprecated-apis.md`; `current-best-practices.md` § GDScript (4.7). **`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` has no core, scripting or tilemap file** (it holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui), so every claim about `Array[String]` encoding, packed-array methods and GDScript cost below is either probed or marked UNVERIFIED. Project ADRs: 0001 to 0010 (§ Related) |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | Packed-array element writes that skip the property setter (4.7); `@abstract` ports (4.5, chosen by ADR-0010) for `LayoutGraphPort`; typed `Array[String]` as a persisted column. No `TileMapLayer`, `Node` or `Resource` API is used by this ADR |
| **Verification Required** | **V1 (probed 2026-10-29, done):** `PackedInt32Array.bsearch(v)` returns the insertion index and, for ties, the first index with `before = true` and one past the last with `before = false`; `PackedInt32Array.insert` and `remove_at` keep order; a value `0xDEADBEEF` stored in a `PackedInt32Array` reads back as `-559038737` and masks to `3735928559`; `var_to_bytes` then `bytes_to_var` returns a typed `Array[String]` still typed and a `PackedInt64Array` exact to 2^40; `PackedStringArray` also round-trips (but ADR-0006 § 1.2 does not allow it in a save, so it is not used); `duplicate()` of a packed array is independent of later element writes. **V2 (UNVERIFIED, spike S1 / SP-ENG-1):** the GDScript cost of the `layout.doors` loop at `MAX_DOORS_LOADED` doors on a release export on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK against its 0.2 ms line (TR-section-042). **V3 (UNVERIFIED, S1 with ADR-0014):** the P2 cost of `attach_section` and `detach_section` including the per-body broadphase rebuild at `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY`. **V4 (UNVERIFIED, after ADR-0005 is Accepted):** golden vectors for `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `structure_hash` of the four MVP templates, equal on the editor and on the `template_release` export (ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1). **V5 (UNVERIFIED):** `Array[String]` column cost in `snapshot()` and in the type walk for the largest long-campaign shape of § 12 (tens of rows; expected negligible, measured in SAVE-WRK-1 f) |

## ADR Dependencies

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Depends On** | ADR-0003 (block descriptor, Class A/B mutators, `WriteScope`, fault domains, owner-callable contract); ADR-0004 (dirty-key layout and `KeySpaceDescriptor`); ADR-0005 (canonical encoding, `Hash64.of_value`, `IntMath`, `low32`, block hash cache); ADR-0006 (snapshot types allowed in a save, two-phase `restore`, `ctx.fault`); ADR-0007 (template catalog, manifests, `section_templates` ledger, boot tiers); ADR-0010 (`src/sim/layout/`, ports, lint tiers, `## @hot`); ADR-0001 and ADR-0002 (P2/P3 phases, hook registration, no Layout command). None is Accepted yet, so this ADR cannot be Accepted before them |
| **Enables** | ADR-0014 (rect set, broadphase, `OccluderSource`), ADR-0015 (Body consumes `frame_shift`, `moved_sections`, `rects[]`, `section_at`), ADR-0016 (restore order and verifiers over this block), ADR-0017 (Emitter reads `version`/`static_version`, `anchor_geometry`), ADR-0021 (the weld transaction calls LM2/LM3), ADR-0026 (`init_world` calls LM1), ADR-0034 (PROJECTOR inputs and `entity_id` fields), ADR-0020, ADR-0023, ADR-0027 (read views) |
| **Blocks** | The Layout epic (template compile and hashes, `layout.state`, LM1 to LM4, `layout.doors`, read views); every Feature story that calls `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section` or reads `rects_in`/`room_at`/`door_passage` |
| **Ordering Note** | Wave A. ADR-0011 (Graph data model, same wave) must supply the Graph side of § 3 and § 8: the `instantiate_section` return and its contiguity guarantees, the allocation-free `opening` read and the `LayoutGraphPort` implementation (§ Related lists every assumption). ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016 and ADR-0034 are written afterwards and build on the records fixed here. Where this ADR and the Layout GDD differ (§ Related, "GDD sync"), the ADR is the proposal and the GDD is updated to it, not the reverse |

## Context

### Problem Statement

Layout is the project's single answer to "where is it?". Its GDD (LY-1 to LY-35) fixes behaviour in detail but defers seven implementation questions to ADRs: the block shape against immutable templates (ADR-LAY-01), the id split with the Graph (ADR-LAY-05), the field order of the two template-local byte strings (ADR-LAY-06), and four more that belong to siblings. Three of the deferrals have since been overtaken by Foundation ADRs and no longer mean what the GDD says: ADR-0005 forbids owner-written byte layouts, ADR-0006 limits what a snapshot may contain, and ADR-0003 fixes the shape of a Class A mutator. Without one decision, the Layout epic would invent a snapshot shape the type walk may reject, an id scheme that the Graph's `next_*` counters can desynchronise from, and a weld routine whose result depends on argument order.

The decision is needed now because Body, Assembly, Web Map, Emitter and the PROJECTOR all take ids, offsets and rectangle keys from Layout, and a different assumption in any of them (a sparse section id, a body frame origin, a renumbered `idx`) is a save-compatibility defect once the first build leaves the project.

### Constraints

- **The simulation is pure data** (architecture principle 1): `layout.state` is a `RefCounted` of typed fields and packed arrays; no `Node`, no `Resource`, no float anywhere in the module (LY-3 a, LY-31; ADR-0010 `SIM-01`, `SIM-03`, `SIM-10`).
- **Only plain data reaches a save** (ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3): `null`, `bool`, `int` (64-bit), finite `float`, `String`, `Array`, `Dictionary` with `String` or `int` keys, and `PackedByteArray`/`PackedInt32Array`/`PackedInt64Array`. `PackedStringArray`, `Vector2i`, `Rect2i` and `StringName` are rejected by the walk, although ADR-0005's encoder would accept some of them.
- **One encoder, no owner byte writers** (ADR-0005 § 3.1): Layout supplies the shape of a payload and nothing else; `layout_hash()` is the kernel's block hash.
- **Every persisted id is a stable string key, a ledger integer or a Graph type id** (ADR-0007 § 3.1); never an array position of another block, never position-derived (registry `position_derived_persisted_id`).
- **Content is loaded before the kernel exists** (ADR-0007 § 1.7): templates reach `setup()` as a frozen, get-only `SectionTemplates` catalog; packed arrays are never returned from a catalog (§ 1.5).
- **Mutators are Class A with status returns and caller-owned `out` objects** (ADR-0003 § 5); dirty keys are marked explicitly because 4.7 packed-array element writes no longer call a property setter.
- **P2 applies commands, P3 runs hooks** (ADR-0001): a hook sees the same tick's P2 state, and the Graph's door `area` and `door_state` change only in P2 (LY-10).
- **Capacity ceilings** are fixed by the GDD's Tuning Knobs table and registered constants; this ADR enforces them and does not retype their values.
- **Pre-release saves are disposable** (SL-14, ADR-0006 § 2.6); the migration obligation starts when the first build leaves the project, the same moment ADR-0007's ledgers flip to `SHIPPED`.

### Requirements

- Store instances by reference to templates, with a restore policy that refuses a template edit that would corrupt an instance with history (TR-section-004, -007).
- Allocate and never reuse or renumber `section_id`, `body_id`, `room_id`; keep tombstones; persist `graph_ref_base` per instance (TR-section-005, -037).
- Express geometry as half-open integer rectangles with a flags byte on the 24-px grid, translation only (TR-section-010).
- Keep the door leaf as one rectangle derived from the Graph's `area` in the P3 `layout.doors` hook, with correct seeding, unknown-opening and clamp behaviour (TR-section-012, -013, -014, -034, -035, -042).
- Make sockets terminal-state records changed only by LM2/LM3, with a closed first-failure-wins mating predicate (TR-section-018, -019, TR-assembly-025).
- Provide exactly four Class A mutators with pure checks, and weld offsets that do not depend on argument order (TR-section-020, -021).
- Own room identity, `V` and `exposed_tiles`, own no loose-item table, no `visited` bit, no pose (TR-section-027, -028).
- Enforce capacity ceilings and the block-size diagnostic (TR-section-030, TR-derelict-040, TR-webmap-036).
- Publish read views with fixed field names and deterministic order, including CONSOLE anchor records (TR-section-039, TR-derelict-034, TR-horror-031, -032).

### Binding stances respected (registry check, `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`)

| Registered stance | How this ADR conforms |
|---|---|
| `owner_callable_contract`, `block_registration`, `mutator_status` (ADR-0003) | `layout.state`, `layout.doors`, the fault domain and the key space are registered in `BOOTING` through `ModuleFacet.registrar`; the four mutators are Class A, statuses `OK`/`REFUSED`/`-code`, results through `out`. The `can_*` names diverge from the `check_*` example in the registry; the shape does not (§ 9) |
| `dirty_key_marking`, `change_notification` (ADR-0004) | Keys are `(KIND << 32) | id` with kinds SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3 as LY-32 and **one added kind, LEAF 4** (§ 8); `quiet_writes_allowed` is false |
| `canonical_encode_and_hash`, `block_persistence_payload` (ADR-0005, ADR-0006) | The snapshot is a `Dictionary` of named packed arrays; no int-keyed dictionary, no `PackedStringArray`; template hashes are `Hash64.of_value` of three sub-payloads whose shape § 4 fixes |
| `static_content_catalogs`, `id_ledgers` (ADR-0007) | Templates arrive as a frozen `SectionTemplates` through `setup()`; `section_templates` ledger nesting is decided in § 4 |
| `position_derived_persisted_id`, `block_as_resource_or_node`, `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`, `packed_array_exposed_or_setter_tracked` (forbidden patterns) | No id derives from a position; the block is a `RefCounted`; payload arrays are duplicates; dirty marking is explicit |
| `fault_domain_table` | Layout is static domain 4 |

No registered stance is contradicted. Three Foundation texts are read as follows and recorded as asks rather than worked around: ADR-0003 § 5 names the pure check `check_*` (this ADR keeps the GDD's published `can_*` names and the same shape), ADR-0005 § 3.2 lists `PackedStringArray` as encodable while ADR-0006 § 1.2 rejects it in a save (this ADR avoids it), and ADR-0007 § 3.2 describes one id range per ledger space (§ 4 uses one range and a class split by key shape).

## Decision

### Architecture Diagram

```
 content (before the kernel exists)                       kernel BOOTING (ADR-0003)
 ---------------------------------                        ------------------------
 assets/data/sections/*.json  --ADR-0007 stage 3-->  SectionTemplates (frozen, get-only)
   + ids.lock.json (flat pairs)                         |  compiled rect table, rooms, sockets, doors,
   + geometry/visual/structure hashes (once)            |  anchors, slots, 3 hashes per template
                                                        v
                                         LayoutModule.setup(facet, templates, tuning, graph_port)
                                           registers: block layout.state  hook layout.doors
                                                      fault domain 4  key space {SEC,BODY,SEAM,LEAF}
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 RUNNING                             owner object LayoutModule (src/sim/layout/)
                                     +------------------------------+     +----------------------------+
