Register lint rows LAY-SOCKET-01 (no write to layout socket columns outside LM2/LM3) and LAY-ID-01 (no write to Layout counters outside LM1/LM3), add src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd to the ports/port_files list in modules.json, and add Layout's hot-read list (section 11) to the HOT-01 tag list.

decisions.chosen: Add `structure_hash` beside geometry_hash and visual_hash (14 columns, one over the GDD's 13); a structure mismatch refuses restore for every instance, a geometry mismatch only for instances with history
decisions.reason: room_id, comp_base+room_index and socket_index index the current template by position. A reorder keeps every set and count equal, so on a never-welded FREE instance geometry_changed_fresh would silently re-point ids to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's claim that a reorder only affects new instances is wrong. Cost is 4 bytes a row. Flagged for user confirmation (OQ-3).

decisions.chosen: LayoutState (persisted tables) and LayoutDerived (caches, versions, leaf cache, lookups, broadphase handle) under one LayoutModule owner
decisions.reason: Makes 'derived caches never persisted' testable; restore copies into the existing LayoutState so the LayoutViews facade stays valid.

decisions.chosen: Dense ordinals: section_id == row+1 and body_id == row+1; an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; restore verifies it
decisions.reason: Removes id maps from hot reads, makes the dense-id check a restore invariant, and no reserve-an-id path exists. Cost: future sparse-id procgen would need to supersede this ADR.

decisions.chosen: Typed Array[String] column (not PackedStringArray, not the ledger integer)
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 rejects PackedStringArray in a save. The GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and human-readable dumps name the string. Probed 2026-10-29: a typed Array[String] round-trips through var_to_bytes still typed.

decisions.chosen: Native PackedInt64Array columns for welded_at_T and cut_at_T
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 allows full-width int. The halves convention is mandatory only where a value reaches JSON, and T is bounded below 2^53 for the dev dump.

decisions.chosen: Dictionary shape of three sub-payloads hashed by Hash64.of_value, not an owner TLV byte order
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 3.1 forbids owner byte writers and 4.6 already delegates the sub-payload shape to Layout/ADR-0013.

decisions.chosen: One flat pairs[] in the section_templates space with compound keys <template_id> and <template_id>/<room_key>; class split by key shape and id boundary
decisions.reason: Keeps LedgerCheck.verify and the append-only gate generic, makes per-room dormant/retire a per-pair flip, and needs no second file. The integers are not persisted in layout.state.

decisions.chosen: BOOT named invariant (CONTENT_INVARIANT), not only a CI lint
decisions.reason: Weld-offset closure on the 24 grid and broadphase alignment depend on it; a 12-px socket shift must fail the load (TR-derelict-033).

decisions.chosen: The hook opens layout.state once and marks LEAF/<section_id> per changed section; new key kind LEAF 4
decisions.reason: The PROJECTOR must redraw a changed leaf with no tween. A marked key avoids per-frame polling. A separate kind avoids waking Failure & Trail anchors and Lighting static rebuilds through SEC. Cost: touch_serial advances on door-change ticks and invalidates the hash cache on those ticks.

decisions.chosen: Keep the published can_* names with the exact ADR-0003 check shape; results through caller-owned out records (BuildResult, AttachResult, DetachResult); the can_attach preview payload as a separate pure read preview_attach
decisions.reason: 19 TR rows and four GDDs use can_*; ADR-0003 requires status returns and out objects; a bare StringName cannot carry {reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}.

decisions.chosen: Lower body_id survives, roles assigned by body not argument order, welds[] canonicalised, one shared weld_math and DetachPlanner
decisions.reason: Byte-identical block for reversed calls (AC-172), no dissolving of the home ship by a caller mixup, prediction and apply cannot drift.

decisions.chosen: Layout calls the Graph only through an @abstract LayoutGraphPort injected in setup(); Layout allocates section/body/room ids, the Graph allocates node/edge/compartment/seam ids; LM1 reads counters, calls M1, and appends rows and advances counters only on OK
decisions.reason: No compile cycle (ADR-0010), one writer per id space, fail-closed with no partial counter advance.

decisions.chosen: LM1 derives leaves immediately from the Graph's initial areas; LM2 seeds new LEAF closed without reading area; post_restore runs derive_doors
decisions.reason: weld_join starts the opening at area 0, so reads between P2 apply and the first P3 see a solid span with no stale_leaf and no spurious bump (TR-section-034).

decisions.chosen: All ceilings (sections, bodies, id caps, rects, doors, rooms, Graph pre-check) tested in can_build/can_detach before any id is consumed or the Graph is called; MAX_BODIES counted over LIVE bodies; no BODY_FULL reason
decisions.reason: Clean reject in validate instead of a FAULTED apply; no counter wraps; BODY_FULL stays an open question since the MVP roster is far below the per-body rect ceiling.

decisions.chosen: Hot tier allocation-free with scalar results or caller-owned out and tagged ## @hot; cold tier returns immutable record classes; template-only reads precomputed in the catalog row
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0003 section 7 and ADR-0010 HOT-01; supports Horror's per-run read budgets and idempotence across restore.

decisions.chosen: structure mismatch always refuses; geometry mismatch refuses only with history (non-FREE socket, weld row, shared body) else accepts with geometry_changed_fresh and rewrites the hash; visual mismatch accepts and rewrites; validation order fixed with seven steps
decisions.reason: Keeps the GDD's author-friendly fresh-instance edit while closing the reorder hole; first failure wins with named detail.

decisions.chosen: Stamp each section's region with the tick T; reads return NONE when the stamp differs from the current tick, with no end-of-tick clearing
decisions.reason: Layout has no end-of-tick hook and the stamp is allocation-free.

decisions.chosen: Layout guarantees the three entity_id inputs (section_id, closed kind_ordinal vocabulary, template_local_idx below 2^16) and exports no packing helper
decisions.reason: The namespace byte and packing are ADR-0034 / Pipeline (OQ-33); the architecture assigns the Y-sort key namespaces to ADR-0034.

decisions.chosen: Per-section PackedInt64Array columns in LayoutDerived; bump rules owned here, API owned by ADR-0014; reset to 1 on restore
decisions.reason: Avoids int32 overflow on long runs and keeps ADR-0014 free to expose them on OccluderSource.

decisions.chosen: 20 decided here, 12 shared (this ADR decides its half), 3 owned elsewhere
decisions.reason: TR-section-006/007 and derelict-007/008 hand specific content to ADR-0013 in the matrix notes, so they are shared rather than owned elsewhere.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Graph M1 instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out) returns {node_base, edge_base, comp_base} with node, edge and compartment ranges contiguous and in template order, sized from the template alone, and advances its next_section_id to max(section_id)+1.

The Graph facade extends Layout's @abstract LayoutGraphPort and provides a pure check_instantiate(views, template_id)->StringName for the Graph CAPACITY pre-check, callable from Layout's can_build without writing.

An allocation-free opening_into(edge_id, out)->bool read (area, area_max, door_state; false for an unknown edge) valid in P3 after P2 writes, where the opening area_max for a mated hatch is already min(a, b).
weld_join returns seam_id and opening_ids in the order of socket_plan.openings, and seam_openings_into(seam_id, out) reads them back (also after restore) for the opening_leaves map.

section_counts_into(section_id, out) exposes per-section node, edge and compartment counts and graph.next_section_id for Layout's post-restore verification; JoinPlan field layout is what Layout's WeldPlan fills.
No Graph phase writes area or door_state of a template door or mated hatch in P3; only virtual breach and seam-weep openings change in P3, and Layout neither reads nor projects them.

Builds the per-body broadphase from the SectionTemplate compiled rect accessors (idx-indexed; no packed arrays from the catalog), rebuilds on build/attach/detach/restore calls from Layout, owns QueryBuffer/OccluderSource/SolidQuery signatures, and exposes version/static_version/leaf_version whose bump rules are ADR-0013 sections 7 and 8.
Provides the static-footprint overlap primitive used by can_attach GEOM_OVERLAP (all flags, PLATE at full footprint, room tile cells) so the uncached cost target of 2 ms is achievable.

Body's rebase_on_attach/rebase_on_detach consume frame_shift_px, moved_sections and the DetachResult rects[] (pre-cut body frame, 4 ints per rect); Body supplies foot boxes as caller arguments and Layout never reads body.state.

layout.state declares restore_after: [], every restore() completes before any post_restore(), and ADR-0016's verifier list runs Layout's post-restore checks (graph_ref_base resolves, seam_ids resolve, graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id).

The weld/cut transaction calls Graph weld_join/cut_detach, then Layout LM2/LM3, then Body, inside one P2 apply, checking each Class A status; Layout's can_attach/can_detach run in the transaction's validate.

Every set_opening area write for a template door or mated hatch lands in P2 by command (a CLOSING_BLOCKED retry is a SYSTEM-origin command re-submitted each tick); Interaction calls leaf_would_overlap from validate.
Horror's per-run Layout read budgets and its NONE/UNKNOWN handling are Horror's; Layout guarantees only that its reads are pure, idempotent and return explicit NONE sentinels.
Web Map init_world calls LM1 in the INIT scope (the only LM1 caller) and LM4 after the Graph's M4; ADR-0026 enumerates reachable loaded sets against MAX_BODIES.

The PROJECTOR redraws on SEC, BODY, SEAM and LEAF keys; owns the entity_id packing and LAYOUT_ID_NS byte, the per-section tile chunking (BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) and the Y-sort scene shape; Layout supplies the stable inputs only.
The Emitter keys its static layer on static_version, patches leaves on leaf_version, reads changed_region in the same tick, and treats any restore as an unconditional rebuild signal.

toolu_01CXhsabfTRDGukz28Jy4Qqn.summary: ADR-0013 (Proposed, 2026-10-29) fixes the Layout block, geometry and id split. `layout.state` stores instances by reference to frozen catalog templates as dense per-column packed arrays. Rows are addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones are kept, and `template_id` is a typed Array[String] column. A third persisted `structure_hash` (14 columns, one more than the GDD's 13) makes the reorder check exact. Geometry is half-open integer rects with a flags byte in a reserved `idx` space that is never renumbered. Sockets are sparse terminal-state rows written only inside LM2/LM3. Weld offsets are computed on the lower-`body_id` survivor with a canonicalised `welds[]`. Layout allocates section, body and room ids, and the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids. The ledger (OQ-B) is one flat `pairs[]` with compound keys. `layout.doors` marks a new LEAF dirty key. The four Class A mutators keep the published `can_*` names with `out` records. The ADR also covers restore and drift policy, read-view tiers, capacity, and CONSOLE anchors. Probes run 2026-10-29: bsearch, insert, signed int32 hash storage, and typed Array[String] and PackedInt64Array round-trips. All GDScript cost figures are UNVERIFIED and gated by S1.

decisions.chosen: Add `structure_hash` beside geometry_hash and visual_hash (14 columns, one over the GDD's 13); a structure mismatch refuses restore for every instance, a geometry mismatch only for instances with history
decisions.reason: room_id, comp_base+room_index and socket_index index the current template by position. A reorder keeps every set and count equal, so on a never-welded FREE instance geometry_changed_fresh would silently re-point ids to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's claim that a reorder only affects new instances is wrong. Cost is 4 bytes a row. Flagged for user confirmation (OQ-3).

decisions.chosen: LayoutState (persisted tables) and LayoutDerived (caches, versions, leaf cache, lookups, broadphase handle) under one LayoutModule owner
decisions.reason: Makes 'derived caches never persisted' testable; restore copies into the existing LayoutState so the LayoutViews facade stays valid.

decisions.chosen: Dense ordinals: section_id == row+1 and body_id == row+1; an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; restore verifies it
decisions.reason: Removes id maps from hot reads, makes the dense-id check a restore invariant, and no reserve-an-id path exists. Cost: future sparse-id procgen would need to supersede this ADR.

decisions.chosen: Typed Array[String] column (not PackedStringArray, not the ledger integer)
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 rejects PackedStringArray in a save. The GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and human-readable dumps name the string. Probed 2026-10-29: a typed Array[String] round-trips through var_to_bytes still typed.

decisions.chosen: Native PackedInt64Array columns for welded_at_T and cut_at_T
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 allows full-width int. The halves convention is mandatory only where a value reaches JSON, and T is bounded below 2^53 for the dev dump.

decisions.chosen: Dictionary shape of three sub-payloads hashed by Hash64.of_value, not an owner TLV byte order
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 3.1 forbids owner byte writers and 4.6 already delegates the sub-payload shape to Layout/ADR-0013.

decisions.chosen: One flat pairs[] in the section_templates space with compound keys <template_id> and <template_id>/<room_key>; class split by key shape and id boundary
decisions.reason: Keeps LedgerCheck.verify and the append-only gate generic, makes per-room dormant/retire a per-pair flip, and needs no second file. The integers are not persisted in layout.state.

decisions.chosen: BOOT named invariant (CONTENT_INVARIANT), not only a CI lint
decisions.reason: Weld-offset closure on the 24 grid and broadphase alignment depend on it; a 12-px socket shift must fail the load (TR-derelict-033).

decisions.chosen: The hook opens layout.state once and marks LEAF/<section_id> per changed section; new key kind LEAF 4
decisions.reason: The PROJECTOR must redraw a changed leaf with no tween. A marked key avoids per-frame polling. A separate kind avoids waking Failure & Trail anchors and Lighting static rebuilds through SEC. Cost: touch_serial advances on door-change ticks and invalidates the hash cache on those ticks.

decisions.chosen: Keep the published can_* names with the exact ADR-0003 check shape; results through caller-owned out records (BuildResult, AttachResult, DetachResult); the can_attach preview payload as a separate pure read preview_attach
decisions.reason: 19 TR rows and four GDDs use can_*; ADR-0003 requires status returns and out objects; a bare StringName cannot carry {reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}.

decisions.chosen: Lower body_id survives, roles assigned by body not argument order, welds[] canonicalised, one shared weld_math and DetachPlanner
decisions.reason: Byte-identical block for reversed calls (AC-172), no dissolving of the home ship by a caller mixup, prediction and apply cannot drift.

decisions.chosen: Layout calls the Graph only through an @abstract LayoutGraphPort injected in setup(); Layout allocates section/body/room ids, the Graph allocates node/edge/compartment/seam ids; LM1 reads counters, calls M1, and appends rows and advances counters only on OK
decisions.reason: No compile cycle (ADR-0010), one writer per id space, fail-closed with no partial counter advance.

decisions.chosen: LM1 derives leaves immediately from the Graph's initial areas; LM2 seeds new LEAF closed without reading area; post_restore runs derive_doors
decisions.reason: weld_join starts the opening at area 0, so reads between P2 apply and the first P3 see a solid span with no stale_leaf and no spurious bump (TR-section-034).

decisions.chosen: All ceilings (sections, bodies, id caps, rects, doors, rooms, Graph pre-check) tested in can_build/can_detach before any id is consumed or the Graph is called; MAX_BODIES counted over LIVE bodies; no BODY_FULL reason
decisions.reason: Clean reject in validate instead of a FAULTED apply; no counter wraps; BODY_FULL stays an open question since the MVP roster is far below the per-body rect ceiling.

decisions.chosen: Hot tier allocation-free with scalar results or caller-owned out and tagged ## @hot; cold tier returns immutable record classes; template-only reads precomputed in the catalog row
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0003 section 7 and ADR-0010 HOT-01; supports Horror's per-run read budgets and idempotence across restore.

decisions.chosen: structure mismatch always refuses; geometry mismatch refuses only with history (non-FREE socket, weld row, shared body) else accepts with geometry_changed_fresh and rewrites the hash; visual mismatch accepts and rewrites; validation order fixed with seven steps
decisions.reason: Keeps the GDD's author-friendly fresh-instance edit while closing the reorder hole; first failure wins with named detail.

decisions.chosen: Stamp each section's region with the tick T; reads return NONE when the stamp differs from the current tick, with no end-of-tick clearing
decisions.reason: Layout has no end-of-tick hook and the stamp is allocation-free.

decisions.chosen: Layout guarantees the three entity_id inputs (section_id, closed kind_ordinal vocabulary, template_local_idx below 2^16) and exports no packing helper
decisions.reason: The namespace byte and packing are ADR-0034 / Pipeline (OQ-33); the architecture assigns the Y-sort key namespaces to ADR-0034.

decisions.chosen: Per-section PackedInt64Array columns in LayoutDerived; bump rules owned here, API owned by ADR-0014; reset to 1 on restore
decisions.reason: Avoids int32 overflow on long runs and keeps ADR-0014 free to expose them on OccluderSource.

decisions.chosen: 20 decided here, 12 shared (this ADR decides its half), 3 owned elsewhere
decisions.reason: TR-section-006/007 and derelict-007/008 hand specific content to ADR-0013 in the matrix notes, so they are shared rather than owned elsewhere.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Graph M1 instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out) returns {node_base, edge_base, comp_base} with node, edge and compartment ranges contiguous and in template order, sized from the template alone, and advances its next_section_id to max(section_id)+1.

The Graph facade extends Layout's @abstract LayoutGraphPort and provides a pure check_instantiate(views, template_id)->StringName for the Graph CAPACITY pre-check, callable from Layout's can_build without writing.

An allocation-free opening_into(edge_id, out)->bool read (area, area_max, door_state; false for an unknown edge) valid in P3 after P2 writes, where the opening area_max for a mated hatch is already min(a, b).
weld_join returns seam_id and opening_ids in the order of socket_plan.openings, and seam_openings_into(seam_id, out) reads them back (also after restore) for the opening_leaves map.

section_counts_into(section_id, out) exposes per-section node, edge and compartment counts and graph.next_section_id for Layout's post-restore verification; JoinPlan field layout is what Layout's WeldPlan fills.
No Graph phase writes area or door_state of a template door or mated hatch in P3; only virtual breach and seam-weep openings change in P3, and Layout neither reads nor projects them.

Builds the per-body broadphase from the SectionTemplate compiled rect accessors (idx-indexed; no packed arrays from the catalog), rebuilds on build/attach/detach/restore calls from Layout, owns QueryBuffer/OccluderSource/SolidQuery signatures, and exposes version/static_version/leaf_version whose bump rules are ADR-0013 sections 7 and 8.
Provides the static-footprint overlap primitive used by can_attach GEOM_OVERLAP (all flags, PLATE at full footprint, room tile cells) so the uncached cost target of 2 ms is achievable.

Body's rebase_on_attach/rebase_on_detach consume frame_shift_px, moved_sections and the DetachResult rects[] (pre-cut body frame, 4 ints per rect); Body supplies foot boxes as caller arguments and Layout never reads body.state.

layout.state declares restore_after: [], every restore() completes before any post_restore(), and ADR-0016's verifier list runs Layout's post-restore checks (graph_ref_base resolves, seam_ids resolve, graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id).

The weld/cut transaction calls Graph weld_join/cut_detach, then Layout LM2/LM3, then Body, inside one P2 apply, checking each Class A status; Layout's can_attach/can_detach run in the transaction's validate.

Every set_opening area write for a template door or mated hatch lands in P2 by command (a CLOSING_BLOCKED retry is a SYSTEM-origin command re-submitted each tick); Interaction calls leaf_would_overlap from validate.
Horror's per-run Layout read budgets and its NONE/UNKNOWN handling are Horror's; Layout guarantees only that its reads are pure, idempotent and return explicit NONE sentinels.
Web Map init_world calls LM1 in the INIT scope (the only LM1 caller) and LM4 after the Graph's M4; ADR-0026 enumerates reachable loaded sets against MAX_BODIES.

The PROJECTOR redraws on SEC, BODY, SEAM and LEAF keys; owns the entity_id packing and LAYOUT_ID_NS byte, the per-section tile chunking (BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) and the Y-sort scene shape; Layout supplies the stable inputs only.
The Emitter keys its static layer on static_version, patches leaves on leaf_version, reads changed_region in the same tick, and treats any restore as an unconditional rebuild signal.

open_questions: OQ-1: no BODY_FULL reason, so a merged body could exceed MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY. Recommended: keep it out of MVP and add a world lint; reopen with a MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY knob at the Vertical Slice.

OQ-2: requirements-traceability.md line 1367 still lists TR-derelict-034 as 'ADR-0013 + ADR-0007' while row 724 says it was re-tagged to ADR-0013 alone (2026-10-29). The summary table needs the same fix; this author may not edit that file.
OQ-3: the user must confirm the third hash, structure_hash (14 columns instead of the GDD's 13); the alternative is the GDD's two hashes with the reorder defect documented as an authoring rule.
OQ-4: if continuous or stepped doors are introduced (GDD OQ-14 c), the hook's key-per-tick cost advancing touch_serial and the hash cache needs re-measuring.
OQ-5: can ADR-0011 publish a cheap 'openings changed' counter so layout.doors can early-out? Not required for correctness.
The GDScript cost figures for layout.doors (<= 0.2 ms), attach/detach grid rebuild and can_attach (<= 2 ms) are UNVERIFIED and pending S1 / SP-ENG-1 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports.
Golden vectors for geometry_hash, visual_hash and structure_hash of the four MVP templates await ADR-0005 acceptance and ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1.
TR-section-024: the entity_id packing, LAYOUT_ID_NS byte and 453-tile build rate stay with ADR-0034 and the Pipeline; this ADR only guarantees the inputs.

data.summary: ADR-0013 (Proposed, 2026-10-29) fixes the Layout block, geometry and id split. `layout.state` stores instances by reference to frozen catalog templates as dense per-column packed arrays. Rows are addressed by `id - 1`, tombstones are kept, and `template_id` is a typed Array[String] column. A third persisted `structure_hash` (14 columns, one more than the GDD's 13) makes the reorder check exact. Geometry is half-open integer rects with a flags byte in a reserved `idx` space that is never renumbered. Sockets are sparse terminal-state rows written only inside LM2/LM3. Weld offsets are computed on the lower-`body_id` survivor with a canonicalised `welds[]`. Layout allocates section, body and room ids, and the Graph allocates node, edge, compartment and seam ids. The ledger (OQ-B) is one flat `pairs[]` with compound keys. `layout.doors` marks a new LEAF dirty key. The four Class A mutators keep the published `can_*` names with `out` records. The ADR also covers restore and drift policy, read-view tiers, capacity, and CONSOLE anchors. Probes run 2026-10-29: bsearch, insert, signed int32 hash storage, and typed Array[String] and PackedInt64Array round-trips. All GDScript cost figures are UNVERIFIED and gated by S1.

gdd_sync.old: `layout.state` stores instances by reference to templates (bodies table, 13-int section-instance rows, sparse non-FREE socket table, `welds[]`
gdd_sync.new: `layout.state` stores instances by reference to templates (bodies table, 14-column section-instance rows (13 GDD fields plus `structure_hash`), sparse non-FREE socket table, `welds[]`

gdd_sync.old: (13 ints per row, D.21)
gdd_sync.new: (14 columns per row: the 13 listed fields plus `structure_hash`, a u32 stored as int32; ADR-0013 section 2, D.21)

gdd_sync.old: Because the persisted ids are numeric and assigned at build, a template that merely *reorders* rooms changes ids only for NEW instances; existing saves keep theirs.
gdd_sync.new: A template that reorders rooms, sockets, doors, hardpoints or node/edge refs is a STRUCTURAL change: `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `socket_index` and `comp_base + room_index` index the current template by position, so `structure_hash` (ordered key sequences and tile sets) differs and restore refuses it with `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance (ADR-0013 section 4).

gdd_sync.old: the sets of `room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `node_ref`, or any room's tile set differ
gdd_sync.new: the ordered sequences of `room_key`, `socket_key`, `door_key`, `hp_key`, `node_ref`, `edge_ref`, or any room's tile set differ (a third persisted per-instance hash, `structure_hash`, carries this comparison)

gdd_sync.old: `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` per field in a fixed documented order (ADR-LAY-06)
gdd_sync.new: replaced: `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` and `structure_hash` are `Hash64.low32(Hash64.of_value(sub-payload))` of Dictionary sub-payloads of flat PackedInt32Array families in LY-4 field order (ADR-0013 section 4); Layout writes no byte encoder (ADR-0005 3.1)

gdd_sync.old: KIND in {SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3}
gdd_sync.new: KIND in {SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3, LEAF 4}; `layout.doors` marks `LEAF/<section_id>` once per section whose leaf set changed (ADR-0013 section 8)

gdd_sync.old: returns `{section_id, body_id}`
gdd_sync.new: fills a caller-owned `BuildResult {section_id, body_id}` and returns a status (OK, REFUSED, -fault_code); `attach_section`, `detach_section` likewise return `AttachResult` / `DetachResult` through `out`; the `can_attach` preview payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is the separate pure read `preview_attach` (ADR-0013 sections 6, 9)

gdd_sync.old: `bodies{body_id, origin_section_id, state}`, `instances{section_id, template_id, geometry_hash, visual_hash, body_id, offset_px, rot_q, room_id_base, graph_ref_base{node_base, edge_base, comp_base}, discarded}`

foundation_asks.ask: Section 5 and registry `mutator_status`: state that the Class A check prefix is a naming convention, not a lint, and that `can_*` is accepted beside `check_*` provided the shape is pure, takes views plus scalars and returns a StringName with `&""` = OK; Layout publishes can_build/can_attach/can_detach/can_discard because four consumer GDDs and 19 TR rows use those names.

Section 3 MVP families table: the `layout.state` row gains kind LEAF 4 (`LEAF/<section_id>`, marked by the layout.doors hook once per changed section); confirm a HOOK-scope `open_for` plus mark_dirty for a derived-cache-only change is legal and accepted to advance touch_serial.

Section 4.6: replace `template_hash` with three hashes (geometry_hash, visual_hash, structure_hash), cite ADR-0013 section 4 as the sub-payload shape, add golden vectors for the four MVP templates once Accepted; also reconcile section 3.2 (PackedStringArray encodable) with ADR-0006 section 1.2 (not allowed in a save).

Add ADR-0013 to the referenced_by of TR-section-006/007 rows (dense layout and rot_q/template/geometry rejections); confirm a typed `Array[String]` column is acceptable to the type walk and size bounds (SAVE-WRK-1 f); confirm native int64 columns for welded_at_T/cut_at_T.

Close OQ-B with ADR-0013 section 4 (flat pairs with compound keys `<template_id>` and `<template_id>/<room_key>`, one id range, class split by key shape and an id boundary checked by a Layout-owned SectionLedgerCheck in src/data/sections/); section 3.5: add structure_hash beside geometry_hash and visual_hash; section 2.4: list GRID_24, RECT_STRIDE_OVERFLOW, RECT_FLAGS_ILLEGAL, CONSOLE_ROLE_UNSET and area_max > 0 as BOOT named invariants for section templates.

Register lint rows LAY-SOCKET-01 (no write to layout socket columns outside LM2/LM3) and LAY-ID-01 (no write to Layout counters outside LM1/LM3), add src/sim/layout/ports/layout_graph_port.gd to the ports/port_files list in modules.json, and add Layout's hot-read list (section 11) to the HOT-01 tag list.

decisions.chosen: Add `structure_hash` beside geometry_hash and visual_hash (14 columns, one over the GDD's 13); a structure mismatch refuses restore for every instance, a geometry mismatch only for instances with history
decisions.reason: room_id, comp_base+room_index and socket_index index the current template by position. A reorder keeps every set and count equal, so on a never-welded FREE instance geometry_changed_fresh would silently re-point ids to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's claim that a reorder only affects new instances is wrong. Cost is 4 bytes a row. Flagged for user confirmation (OQ-3).

decisions.chosen: LayoutState (persisted tables) and LayoutDerived (caches, versions, leaf cache, lookups, broadphase handle) under one LayoutModule owner
decisions.reason: Makes 'derived caches never persisted' testable; restore copies into the existing LayoutState so the LayoutViews facade stays valid.

decisions.chosen: Dense ordinals: section_id == row+1 and body_id == row+1; an id is consumed only by the call that appends its row; restore verifies it
decisions.reason: Removes id maps from hot reads, makes the dense-id check a restore invariant, and no reserve-an-id path exists. Cost: future sparse-id procgen would need to supersede this ADR.

decisions.chosen: Typed Array[String] column (not PackedStringArray, not the ledger integer)
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 rejects PackedStringArray in a save. The GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and human-readable dumps name the string. Probed 2026-10-29: a typed Array[String] round-trips through var_to_bytes still typed.

decisions.chosen: Native PackedInt64Array columns for welded_at_T and cut_at_T
decisions.reason: ADR-0006 section 1.2 allows full-width int. The halves convention is mandatory only where a value reaches JSON, and T is bounded below 2^53 for the dev dump.

decisions.chosen: Dictionary shape of three sub-payloads hashed by Hash64.of_value, not an owner TLV byte order
decisions.reason: ADR-0005 3.1 forbids owner byte writers and 4.6 already delegates the sub-payload shape to Layout/ADR-0013.

decisions.chosen: One flat pairs[] in the section_templates space with compound keys <template_id> and <template_id>/<room_key>; class split by key shape and id boundary
decisions.reason: Keeps LedgerCheck.verify and the append-only gate generic, makes per-room dormant/retire a per-pair flip, and needs no second file. The integers are not persisted in layout.state.

decisions.chosen: BOOT named invariant (CONTENT_INVARIANT), not only a CI lint
decisions.reason: Weld-offset closure on the 24 grid and broadphase alignment depend on it; a 12-px socket shift must fail the load (TR-derelict-033).

decisions.chosen: The hook opens layout.state once and marks LEAF/<section_id> per changed section; new key kind LEAF 4
decisions.reason: The PROJECTOR must redraw a changed leaf with no tween. A marked key avoids per-frame polling. A separate kind avoids waking Failure & Trail anchors and Lighting static rebuilds through SEC. Cost: touch_serial advances on door-change ticks and invalidates the hash cache on those ticks.

decisions.chosen: Keep the published can_* names with the exact ADR-0003 check shape; results through caller-owned out records (BuildResult, AttachResult, DetachResult); the can_attach preview payload as a separate pure read preview_attach
decisions.reason: 19 TR rows and four GDDs use can_*; ADR-0003 requires status returns and out objects; a bare StringName cannot carry {reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}.

decisions.chosen: Lower body_id survives, roles assigned by body not argument order, welds[] canonicalised, one shared weld_math and DetachPlanner
decisions.reason: Byte-identical block for reversed calls (AC-172), no dissolving of the home ship by a caller mixup, prediction and apply cannot drift.

decisions.chosen: Layout calls the Graph only through an @abstract LayoutGraphPort injected in setup(); Layout allocates section/body/room ids, the Graph allocates node/edge/compartment/seam ids; LM1 reads counters, calls M1, and appends rows and advances counters only on OK
decisions.reason: No compile cycle (ADR-0010), one writer per id space, fail-closed with no partial counter advance.

decisions.chosen: LM1 derives leaves immediately from the Graph's initial areas; LM2 seeds new LEAF closed without reading area; post_restore runs derive_doors
decisions.reason: weld_join starts the opening at area 0, so reads between P2 apply and the first P3 see a solid span with no stale_leaf and no spurious bump (TR-section-034).

decisions.chosen: All ceilings (sections, bodies, id caps, rects, doors, rooms, Graph pre-check) tested in can_build/can_detach before any id is consumed or the Graph is called; MAX_BODIES counted over LIVE bodies; no BODY_FULL reason
decisions.reason: Clean reject in validate instead of a FAULTED apply; no counter wraps; BODY_FULL stays an open question since the MVP roster is far below the per-body rect ceiling.

decisions.chosen: Hot tier allocation-free with scalar results or caller-owned out and tagged ## @hot; cold tier returns immutable record classes; template-only reads precomputed in the catalog row
decisions.reason: Matches ADR-0003 section 7 and ADR-0010 HOT-01; supports Horror's per-run read budgets and idempotence across restore.

decisions.chosen: structure mismatch always refuses; geometry mismatch refuses only with history (non-FREE socket, weld row, shared body) else accepts with geometry_changed_fresh and rewrites the hash; visual mismatch accepts and rewrites; validation order fixed with seven steps
decisions.reason: Keeps the GDD's author-friendly fresh-instance edit while closing the reorder hole; first failure wins with named detail.

decisions.chosen: Stamp each section's region with the tick T; reads return NONE when the stamp differs from the current tick, with no end-of-tick clearing
decisions.reason: Layout has no end-of-tick hook and the stamp is allocation-free.

decisions.chosen: Layout guarantees the three entity_id inputs (section_id, closed kind_ordinal vocabulary, template_local_idx below 2^16) and exports no packing helper
decisions.reason: The namespace byte and packing are ADR-0034 / Pipeline (OQ-33); the architecture assigns the Y-sort key namespaces to ADR-0034.

decisions.chosen: Per-section PackedInt64Array columns in LayoutDerived; bump rules owned here, API owned by ADR-0014; reset to 1 on restore
decisions.reason: Avoids int32 overflow on long runs and keeps ADR-0014 free to expose them on OccluderSource.

decisions.chosen: 20 decided here, 12 shared (this ADR decides its half), 3 owned elsewhere
decisions.reason: TR-section-006/007 and derelict-007/008 hand specific content to ADR-0013 in the matrix notes, so they are shared rather than owned elsewhere.

cross_adr_assumptions.assumption: Graph M1 instantiate_section(scope, section_id, template_id, kind, out) returns {node_base, edge_base, comp_base} with node, edge and compartment ranges contiguous and in template order, sized from the template alone, and advances its next_section_id to max(section_id)+1.

The Graph facade extends Layout's @abstract LayoutGraphPort and provides a pure check_instantiate(views, template_id)->StringName for the Graph CAPACITY pre-check, callable from Layout's can_build without writing.

An allocation-free opening_into(edge_id, out)->bool read (area, area_max, door_state; false for an unknown edge) valid in P3 after P2 writes, where the opening area_max for a mated hatch is already min(a, b).
weld_join returns seam_id and opening_ids in the order of socket_plan.openings, and seam_openings_into(seam_id, out) reads them back (also after restore) for the opening_leaves map.

section_counts_into(section_id, out) exposes per-section node, edge and compartment counts and graph.next_section_id for Layout's post-restore verification; JoinPlan field layout is what Layout's WeldPlan fills.
No Graph phase writes area or door_state of a template door or mated hatch in P3; only virtual breach and seam-weep openings change in P3, and Layout neither reads nor projects them.

Builds the per-body broadphase from the SectionTemplate compiled rect accessors (idx-indexed; no packed arrays from the catalog), rebuilds on build/attach/detach/restore calls from Layout, owns QueryBuffer/OccluderSource/SolidQuery signatures, and exposes version/static_version/leaf_version whose bump rules are ADR-0013 sections 7 and 8.
Provides the static-footprint overlap primitive used by can_attach GEOM_OVERLAP (all flags, PLATE at full footprint, room tile cells) so the uncached cost target of 2 ms is achievable.

Body's rebase_on_attach/rebase_on_detach consume frame_shift_px, moved_sections and the DetachResult rects[] (pre-cut body frame, 4 ints per rect); Body supplies foot boxes as caller arguments and Layout never reads body.state.

layout.state declares restore_after: [], every restore() completes before any post_restore(), and ADR-0016's verifier list runs Layout's post-restore checks (graph_ref_base resolves, seam_ids resolve, graph.next_section_id == layout.next_section_id).

The weld/cut transaction calls Graph weld_join/cut_detach, then Layout LM2/LM3, then Body, inside one P2 apply, checking each Class A status; Layout's can_attach/can_detach run in the transaction's validate.

Every set_opening area write for a template door or mated hatch lands in P2 by command (a CLOSING_BLOCKED retry is a SYSTEM-origin command re-submitted each tick); Interaction calls leaf_would_overlap from validate.
Horror's per-run Layout read budgets and its NONE/UNKNOWN handling are Horror's; Layout guarantees only that its reads are pure, idempotent and return explicit NONE sentinels.
Web Map init_world calls LM1 in the INIT scope (the only LM1 caller) and LM4 after the Graph's M4; ADR-0026 enumerates reachable loaded sets against MAX_BODIES.

The PROJECTOR redraws on SEC, BODY, SEAM and LEAF keys; owns the entity_id packing and LAYOUT_ID_NS byte, the per-section tile chunking (BUILD_TILES_PER_FRAME) and the Y-sort scene shape; Layout supplies the stable inputs only.
The Emitter keys its static layer on static_version, patches leaves on leaf_version, reads changed_region in the same tick, and treats any restore as an unconditional rebuild signal.

open_questions: OQ-1: no BODY_FULL reason, so a merged body could exceed MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY. Recommended: keep it out of MVP and add a world lint; reopen with a MAX_SECTIONS_PER_BODY knob at the Vertical Slice.

OQ-2: requirements-traceability.md line 1367 still lists TR-derelict-034 as 'ADR-0013 + ADR-0007' while row 724 says it was re-tagged to ADR-0013 alone (2026-10-29). The summary table needs the same fix; this author may not edit that file.
OQ-3: the user must confirm the third hash, structure_hash (14 columns instead of the GDD's 13); the alternative is the GDD's two hashes with the reorder defect documented as an authoring rule.
OQ-4: if continuous or stepped doors are introduced (GDD OQ-14 c), the hook's key-per-tick cost advancing touch_serial and the hash cache needs re-measuring.
OQ-5: can ADR-0011 publish a cheap 'openings changed' counter so layout.doors can early-out? Not required for correctness.
The GDScript cost figures for layout.doors (<= 0.2 ms), attach/detach grid rebuild and can_attach (<= 2 ms) are UNVERIFIED and pending S1 / SP-ENG-1 on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release exports.
Golden vectors for geometry_hash, visual_hash and structure_hash of the four MVP templates await ADR-0005 acceptance and ADR-0007 CONTENT-EXP-1.
TR-section-024: the entity_id packing, LAYOUT_ID_NS byte and 453-tile build rate stay with ADR-0034 and the Pipeline; this ADR only guarantees the inputs.
